title.zh: 卷42 列傳第7 李德林
title.raw: 卷42 列傳第7 李德林 Volume 42 Biographies 7: Li Delin

sentences.zh: 李德林李德林，字公輔，博陵安平人也。

translations.literal: Li Delin, styled Gongfu, was a native of Anping in Boling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Li Delin, whose courtesy name was Gongfu, came from Anping in Boling.

sentences.zh: 祖壽，湖州戶曹從事。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shou served as Registrar of the Household Bureau in Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shou had been a registrar in the household bureau of Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 父敬族，曆太學博士、鎮遠將軍。

translations.literal: His father Jingzu successively held the posts of Erudite of the Imperial Academy and General Who Pacifies the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jingzu served in turn as erudite of the Imperial Academy and as General Who Pacifies the Distance.

sentences.zh: 魏孝靜帝時，命當世通人正定文籍，以為內校書，別在直閤省。

translations.literal: During the reign of Emperor Xiaojing of Wei, when the foremost experts of the age were ordered to collate the literary canon, he was made Inner Collator of Texts and was separately stationed in the Direct Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaojing of Wei, when leading scholars were summoned to collate the canon, Jingzu was appointed inner collator of texts and attached to the Direct Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 德林幼聰敏，年數歲，誦左思《蜀都賦》，十餘日便度。

translations.literal: Delin was clever from childhood; at only a few years of age he recited Zuo Si's Rhapsody on the Shu Capital and mastered it within little more than ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Delin showed precocious intelligence: at only a few years old he committed Zuo Si's Rhapsody on the Shu Capital to memory in little more than ten days.

sentences.zh: 高隆之見而嗟歎，遍告朝士，雲：「若假其年，必為天下偉器。

translations.literal: Gao Longzhi saw him and sighed in admiration, telling all the court officials: "If granted years, he will surely become a great vessel of the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Longzhi marveled at him and spread word among the courtiers: "Given time, this boy will become one of the great pillars of the empire."

sentences.zh: 」鄴京人士多就宅觀之，月余，日中車馬不絕。

translations.literal: Many people in the capital of Ye came to his house to observe him; for more than a month, carriages and horses passed without cease even at midday.
translations.idiomatic: For more than a month curious visitors from Ye thronged his home, and at midday the street before his gate never lacked horses and carriages.

sentences.zh: 年十五，誦五經及古今文集，日數千言。

translations.literal: At fifteen he could recite the Five Classics and collections of ancient and modern writings, several thousand words per day.
translations.idiomatic: By fifteen he was reciting the Five Classics and anthologies old and new at a rate of several thousand characters a day.

sentences.zh: 俄而該博墳典，陰陽緯候，無不通涉。

translations.literal: Before long he had mastered the breadth of canonical texts, yin-yang lore, weft writings, and astronomical portents, leaving none unexplored.
translations.idiomatic: He soon mastered the classical canon, yin-yang theory, apocryphal weft texts, and calendrical astrology with equal thoroughness.

sentences.zh: 善屬文，辭核而理暢。

translations.literal: He excelled at literary composition; his diction was concise and his reasoning lucid.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote with skill—his language taut, his argument clear.

sentences.zh: 魏收嘗對高隆之謂其父曰：「賢子文筆終當繼溫子升。

translations.literal: Wei Shou once said to his father in Gao Longzhi's presence: "Your worthy son's brushwork will ultimately succeed Wen Zisheng's."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou once told his father in Gao Longzhi's hearing, "Your son's literary talent will one day take up where Wen Zisheng left off."

sentences.zh: 」隆之大笑曰：「魏常侍殊已嫉賢，何不近比老彭，乃遠求溫子！

translations.literal: Longzhi laughed loudly and said: "Vice Censor Wei is truly jealous of talent—why not compare him to the close example of Old Peng rather than reach far for Master Wen!"
translations.idiomatic: Longzhi laughed aloud: "Vice Censor Wei is jealous of other men's gifts. Compare the boy to Old Peng close at hand—why reach all the way to Wen Zisheng?"

sentences.zh: 」年十六，遭父艱，自駕靈輿，反葬故里。

translations.literal: At sixteen he encountered his father's mourning; he himself drove the funeral carriage and returned to bury him in his native place.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen, when his father died, he drove the bier himself and bore the body home for burial.

sentences.zh: 時正嚴冬，單衰跣足，州裡人物由是敬慕之。

translations.literal: It was the depth of winter; wearing only a thin mourning garment, he went barefoot, and the people of the prefecture therefore revered him.
translations.idiomatic: It was deep winter, yet he wore only thin mourning garb and went barefoot—and for this the people of the district came to admire him.

sentences.zh: 博陵豪族有崔諶者，僕射之兄，因休假還鄉，車服甚盛。

translations.literal: Among the great clans of Boling was one Cui Chen, elder brother of a Grand Master of Works, who on returning home for leave had very splendid carriage and attire.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Chen of the great Boling clan, elder brother of a grand master of works, came home on leave with an imposing train of carriage and attendants.

sentences.zh: 將從其宅詣德林赴吊，相去十餘裡，從者數十騎，稍稍減留。

translations.literal: About to go from his house to Delin's to offer condolences, with more than ten li between them and several dozen riders in his train, he gradually sent men back.
translations.idiomatic: When he set out from his estate to offer condolences at Delin's, more than ten li away, his dozens of mounted escorts were dismissed little by little along the road.

sentences.zh: 比至德林門，才餘五騎，雲不得令李生怪人燻灼。

translations.literal: By the time he reached Delin's gate, only five riders remained; he said one must not let Master Li find people oppressively dazzling.
translations.idiomatic: By Delin's gate only five horsemen remained; Cui said he must not let young Li think his guests were putting on grand airs.

sentences.zh: 德林居貧轗軻，母氏多疾，方留心典籍，無複宦情。

translations.literal: Delin lived in poverty and hardship; his mother suffered frequent illness, and he was then absorbed in canonical texts, with no further desire for office.
translations.idiomatic: Delin lived in poverty while his mother lay often ill; immersed in his books, he had no taste left for official life.

sentences.zh: 其後，母病稍愈，逼令仕進。

translations.literal: Afterward, when his mother's illness improved somewhat, she compelled him to enter official service.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother recovered somewhat, she pressed him to seek an appointment.

sentences.zh: 任城王湝為定州刺史，重其才，召入州館。

translations.literal: Prince of Rencheng Jian served as Governor of Dingzhou, prized his talent, and summoned him into the provincial mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian of Rencheng, then governor of Dingzhou, valued his gifts and brought him into the provincial residence.

sentences.zh: 朝夕同游，殆均師友，不為君民禮數。

translations.literal: They associated together morning and evening, nearly as teacher and friend, without observing the etiquette between lord and subject.
translations.idiomatic: They spent their days together almost as equals, master and friend, heedless of court etiquette between prince and subject.

sentences.zh: 嘗語德林雲：「竊聞蔽賢蒙顯戮。

translations.literal: He once said to Delin: "I have heard that concealing the worthy brings conspicuous punishment."
translations.idiomatic: He once told Delin, "They say that whoever hides talent from the throne earns a notorious punishment."

sentences.zh: 久令君沈滯，吾獨得潤身，朝廷縱不見尤，亦懼明靈所譴。

translations.literal: Long have I kept you sunk in obscurity while I alone have enriched myself; even if the court does not blame me, I still fear reproach from the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: I have kept you stuck in obscurity while I alone prosper. Even if the court never censures me, I still dread the spirits' judgment.

sentences.zh: 」於是舉秀才入鄴，于時天保八年也。

translations.literal: With this he recommended him as a xiucai to enter Ye; it was the eighth year of Tianbao.
translations.idiomatic: He then presented Delin as a provincial graduate candidate to Ye—in the eighth year of Tianbao.

sentences.zh: 王因遺尚書令楊遵彥書雲：「燕趙固多奇士，此言誠不為謬。

translations.literal: The prince thereupon sent a letter to Director of the Masters of Writing Yang Zunyan saying: "Yan and Zhao have always abounded in remarkable men—this saying is truly no error."
translations.idiomatic: The prince wrote Yang Zunyan, director of the masters of writing: "That Yan and Zhao breed extraordinary men is no empty boast."

sentences.zh: 今歲所貢秀才李德林者，文章學識，固不待言，觀其風神器宇，終為棟樑之用。

translations.literal: The xiucai presented this year, Li Delin, need hardly be praised for literary learning—yet judging his bearing and stature, he will ultimately serve as pillar timber.
translations.idiomatic: This year's candidate Li Delin scarcely needs praise for learning or literary skill; his presence alone marks him as a future pillar of the state.

sentences.zh: 至如經國大體，是賈生、晁錯之儔；

translations.literal: As for governing the state in broad outline, he is the peer of Jia Yi and Chao Cuo;
translations.idiomatic: On the great questions of statecraft he belongs with Jia Yi and Chao Cuo;

sentences.zh: 雕蟲小技，殆相如、子雲之輩。

translations.literal: in petty ornamental craft he nearly belongs with Sima Xiangru and Yang Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: in literary ornament he ranks with Sima Xiangru and Yang Xiong.

sentences.zh: 今雖唐、虞君世，俊乂盈朝，然修大廈者，豈厭夫良材之積也？

translations.literal: Though today we have generations like those of Tang and Yu, with the talented filling the court, yet those who build great halls—do they ever grow weary of piling up fine timber?
translations.idiomatic: Even in an age of Yao and Shun, with worthies crowding court, builders of great halls never begrudge another load of good timber.

sentences.zh: 吾嘗見孔文舉《薦禰衡表》雲：'洪水橫流，帝思俾乂。

translations.literal: I once saw Kong Wenju's Memorial Recommending Mi Heng, which says: 'Floods rage across the land, and the Emperor thinks of those who might govern.'
translations.idiomatic: I once read Kong Rong's memorial for Mi Heng: 'Floods spread wide, and the Emperor longs for men who can govern.'

sentences.zh: '以正平比夫大禹，常謂擬諭非倫。

translations.literal: To compare Zhengping to Yu the Great—I always thought such a simile was inapt.
translations.idiomatic: Comparing Zhengping to Yu the Great always struck me as a poor likeness.

sentences.zh: 今以德林言之，便覺前言非大。

translations.literal: Speaking now of Delin, I feel the earlier praise was not excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Set against Delin, that old praise now seems almost restrained.

sentences.zh: 」遵彥即命德林制《讓尚書令表》，援筆立成，不加治點。

translations.literal: Zunyan immediately ordered Delin to compose a Memorial Declining the Directorate of the Masters of Writing; he took up the brush and finished it at once without revision.
translations.idiomatic: Zunyan at once asked him to draft a memorial declining the directorship; Delin wrote it in a single sitting without a single correction.

sentences.zh: 因大相賞異，以示吏部郎中陸卬。

translations.literal: He thereupon admired him greatly and showed it to Lu Ang, Bureau Director of the Ministry of Civil Service Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zunyan was deeply impressed and showed the draft to Lu Ang of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 卬雲：「已大見其文筆，浩浩如長河東注。

translations.literal: Ang said: "I had already seen his literary brushwork—vast as a great river pouring eastward."
translations.idiomatic: Ang said, "I already knew his pen could roll like a great river eastward."

sentences.zh: 比來所見，後生製作，乃涓澮之流耳。

translations.literal: By comparison, what I have seen of recent younger authors are merely trickling rivulets.
translations.idiomatic: Beside him, everything young writers have produced lately is a mere creek.

sentences.zh: 」卬仍命其子乂與德林周旋，戒之曰：「汝每事宜師此人，以為模楷。

translations.literal: Ang then ordered his son Yi to associate with Delin and admonished him: "In every matter you should take this man as your teacher and make him your model."
translations.idiomatic: Ang had his son Yi keep company with Delin and warned him, "Take this man as your model in all things."

sentences.zh: 」時遵彥銓衡，深慎選舉，秀才擢第，罕有甲科。

translations.literal: At that time Zunyan oversaw selection and was deeply cautious in appointments; among xiucai elevated to degrees, top grades were rare.
translations.idiomatic: Zunyan ran selection with stern care, and top honors among graduates were rare.

sentences.zh: 德林射策五條，考皆為上，授殿中將軍。

translations.literal: Delin answered five policy questions in the archery ceremony; all examinations were graded highest, and he was appointed Palace Interior General.
translations.idiomatic: Delin answered five policy questions, earned top marks on every paper, and was made palace interior general.

sentences.zh: 既是西省散員，非其所好，又以天保季世，乃謝病還鄉，闔門守道。

translations.literal: Since it was a loose post in the Western Secretariat, not to his liking, and moreover because it was the late Tianbao period, he pleaded illness and returned home, shutting his gate to keep to the Way.
translations.idiomatic: The post was an idle berth in the Western Secretariat, not to his taste; with Tianbao in its decline he pleaded illness, went home, and shut his door to the world.

sentences.zh: 乾明初，遵彥奏追德林入議曹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianming, Zunyan memorialized to recall Delin into the Discussion Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianming era Zunyan had Delin recalled to the Discussion Bureau.

sentences.zh: 皇建初，下詔搜揚人物，複追赴晉陽。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangjian an edict was issued to seek out and promote men of talent; he was again summoned to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Huangjian began, an edict called for talent and Delin was summoned again to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 撰《春思賦》一篇，代稱典麗。

translations.literal: He composed a piece entitled Rhapsody on Spring Longing, acclaimed in the age as a canonical masterpiece of elegance.
translations.idiomatic: His Rhapsody on Spring Longing was acclaimed in its day as a model of elegant writing.

sentences.zh: 是時長廣王作相，居守在鄴。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Chaguang served as Chancellor and remained on guard in Ye.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Chaguang was then chancellor, stationed at Ye.

sentences.zh: 敕德林還京，與散騎常侍高元海等參掌機密。

translations.literal: Delin was ordered back to the capital to join Attendant Cavalier Gao Yuanhai and others in managing confidential matters.
translations.idiomatic: Delin was ordered back to the capital to handle secrets alongside attendant cavalier Gao Yuanhai and others.

sentences.zh: 王引授丞相府行參軍。

translations.literal: The prince brought him in and appointed him Acting Vice Colonel in the Chancellor's Mansion.
translations.idiomatic: The prince took him on as acting administrative assistant in the chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 未幾而王即帝位，授奉朝請，寓直舍人省。

translations.literal: Before long the prince ascended the imperial throne and appointed him Court For the Dynasty, lodging on duty in the Secretariat of Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the prince became emperor and made Delin court for the dynasty, with lodging duty in the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 河清中，授員外散騎侍郎，帶齋帥，仍別直機密省。

translations.literal: During Heqing he was made Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier and carried the title of Fast Director, still separately on duty in the Bureau of Secrets.
translations.idiomatic: In the Heqing era he became supernumerary attendant cavalier and fast director, with separate watch in the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 天統初，授給事中，直中書，參掌詔誥。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiantong he was made Supervisor of Attendants, on duty in the Secretariat, participating in edicts and proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tiantong he was made supervisor of attendants at the secretariat, drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 尋遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 武平初，加通直散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wuping he was additionally given the title of Vice Director of Attendants Cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wuping he was further made vice director of attendants cavalier.

sentences.zh: 又敕與中書侍郎宋士素、副侍中趙彥深別典機密。

translations.literal: He was further ordered together with Secretariat Vice Director Song Shisu and Vice Palace Attendant Zhao Yanshen to separately administer confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was then ordered with Song Shisu and Zhao Yanshen to handle confidential affairs separately.

sentences.zh: 尋丁母艱去職，勺飲不入口五日。

translations.literal: Soon he left office upon his mother's death and took no spoonful of drink for five days.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, his mother's death forced him from office; for five days he took not even a spoonful of water.

sentences.zh: 因發熱病，遍體生瘡，而哀泣不絕。

translations.literal: He thereupon developed a feverish illness, sores erupted over his entire body, yet his weeping of grief did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Fever followed; sores covered his body, yet his mourning tears never stopped.

sentences.zh: 諸士友陸騫、宋士素，名醫張子彥等，為合湯藥。

translations.literal: His gentleman friends Lu Qian, Song Shisu, the famous physician Zhang Ziyan, and others prepared medicinal broths for him.
translations.idiomatic: Friends Lu Qian and Song Shisu and the physician Zhang Ziyan among others brewed medicines for him.

sentences.zh: 德林不肯進，遍體洪腫，數日間，一時頓差，身力平復。

translations.literal: Delin refused to take them; his whole body swelled enormously, yet within several days he suddenly recovered completely and his strength returned to normal.
translations.idiomatic: Delin refused the medicines; his body swelled terribly, then within days the swelling vanished and his strength returned.

sentences.zh: 諸人皆雲孝感所致。

translations.literal: All the men said this was brought about by filial devotion moving Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone said filial piety had moved heaven.

sentences.zh: 太常博士巴叔仁表上其事，朝廷嘉之。

translations.literal: Erudite of the Grand Ceremonial Ba Shuren memorialized the matter upward, and the court commended it.
translations.idiomatic: Ba Shuren of the Board of Ceremonies reported the affair and the court praised him.

sentences.zh: 才滿百日，奪情起複，德林以羸病屬疾，請急罷歸。

translations.literal: When the hundred days were barely complete, mourning leave was cut short and he was recalled; Delin, being frail and still ill, urgently requested to be dismissed and return.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had the hundred days passed when he was recalled from mourning; frail and still sick, Delin pleaded to be sent home.

sentences.zh: 魏收與陽休之論《齊書》起元事，敕集百司會議。

translations.literal: Wei Shou and Yang Xiuzhi debated the matter of establishing the inaugural year in the Book of Qi, and an edict ordered all offices to assemble for conference.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Shou and Yang Xiuzhi disputed how the Book of Qi should date its opening year, an edict convened officials from every bureau.

sentences.zh: 收與德林書曰：「前者議文，總諸事意，小如混漫，難可領解。

translations.literal: Shou wrote to Delin: "The earlier discussion text, gathering all the points at issue, seems somewhat muddled and hard to grasp at a glance."
translations.idiomatic: Shou wrote Delin: "The earlier discussion lumps every point together; it reads muddy and is hard to follow."

sentences.zh: 今便隨事條列，幸為留懷，細加推逐。

translations.literal: I now set them out item by item according to the issues; I hope you will keep them in mind and examine them closely point by point.
translations.idiomatic: I have listed each issue below; please read them carefully and work through each in turn.

sentences.zh: 凡言或者，皆是敵人之議。

translations.literal: Whatever is said with "perhaps" is all the argument of opponents.
translations.idiomatic: Every tentative objection I cite comes from our opponents.

sentences.zh: 既聞人說，因而探論耳。

translations.literal: Having heard people speak of them, I therefore explore and discuss them—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: I raise them only because I have heard others say so.

sentences.zh: 」德林複書曰：「即位之元，《春秋》常義。

translations.literal: Delin replied in a letter: "The inaugural year of accession is the regular principle of the Spring and Autumn Annals."
translations.idiomatic: Delin wrote back: "Dating a reign from its inaugural year is standard Spring and Autumn practice."

sentences.zh: 謹按魯君息姑不稱即位，亦有元年，非獨即位得稱元年也。

translations.literal: I respectfully note that Duke Xigang of Lu was not styled as having acceded, yet there is still a first year—it is not only upon accession that one may be called first year.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xigang of Lu is never said to have acceded, yet his chronicle still opens with a first year—so the inaugural year need not mean accession alone.

sentences.zh: 議雲受終之元，《尚書》之古典。

translations.literal: The discussion says the inaugural year of receiving the end is an ancient canon of the Documents.
translations.idiomatic: One objection calls the inaugural year of receiving the mandate an ancient rule of the Documents.

sentences.zh: 謹按《大傳》，周公攝政，一年救亂，二年伐殷，三年踐奄，四年建侯衛，五年營成周，六年制禮作樂，七年致政成王。

translations.literal: I respectfully note that according to the Great Tradition, the Duke of Zhou acted as regent: in the first year he rescued disorder; in the second he campaigned against Yin; in the third he suppressed Yan; in the fourth he enfeoffed the lords of Wei; in the fifth he built Chengzhou; in the sixth he established rites and made music; in the seventh he returned government to King Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Tradition says the Duke of Zhou as regent: year one, quelled disorder; year two, attacked Yin; year three, suppressed Yan; year four, enfeoffed Wei; year five, built Chengzhou; year six, made rites and music; year seven, restored King Cheng.

sentences.zh: 論者或以舜、禹受終，是為天子。

translations.literal: Discussants sometimes take Shun and Yu receiving the end as becoming Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Some argue that when Shun and Yu received the mandate they were already Sons of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 然則周公以臣禮而死，此亦稱元，非獨受終為帝也。

translations.literal: Yet the Duke of Zhou died in the rites of a subject, and this too is called inaugural year—it is not only upon receiving the end and becoming emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Duke of Zhou died still a subject, and his regency is still dated by an inaugural year—so the inaugural year does not require full imperial status.

sentences.zh: 蒙示議文，扶病省覽，荒情迷識，暫得發蒙。

translations.literal: Receiving your shown discussion text, I perused it while supporting my illness; my benighted feelings and confused understanding have for the moment been enlightened.
translations.idiomatic: I have read your discussion, ill as I am, and your arguments have briefly cleared my confusion.

sentences.zh: 當世君子，必無橫議，唯應閣筆贊成而已。

translations.literal: The gentlemen of the age will surely offer no contrary argument; they should only lay down their brushes and approve.
translations.idiomatic: No gentleman of our day will gainsay you; they should simply lay down their brushes and assent.

sentences.zh: 輒謂前二條有益於議，仰見議中不錄，謹以寫呈。

translations.literal: I venture to say the first two points benefit the discussion; seeing they are not recorded in the discussion, I respectfully copy and present them.
translations.idiomatic: I believe the first two points strengthen your case; as they are missing from your draft, I copy them here for you.

sentences.zh: 」收重遺書曰：「惠示二事，感佩殊深。

translations.literal: Shou sent another letter: "You kindly showed me two matters; I am deeply moved and grateful."
translations.idiomatic: Shou wrote again: "Thank you for the two points—I am deeply obliged."

sentences.zh: 以魯公諸侯之事，昨小為疑。

translations.literal: Regarding the matter of the Duke of Lu as a feudal lord, I had a small doubt yesterday.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday I still had a small doubt about the Duke of Lu as a feudal lord.

sentences.zh: 息姑不書即位，舜、禹亦不言即位。

translations.literal: Xigang is not recorded as having acceded; Shun and Yu likewise are not said to have acceded.
translations.idiomatic: Xigang's accession is not recorded, nor are Shun's or Yu's.

sentences.zh: 息姑雖攝，尚得書元，舜、禹之攝稱元，理也。

translations.literal: Though Xigang was regent, he could still be written as inaugural year; that Shun and Yu as regents should be called inaugural year is reasonable.
translations.idiomatic: Though Xigang only regented, his chronicle still uses the inaugural year; the same logic applies to Shun and Yu as regents.

sentences.zh: 周公居攝，乃雲一年救亂，似不稱元。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou held the regency, yet it says 'in the first year he rescued disorder'—it seems not to call it inaugural year.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou as regent is dated 'year one, rescued disorder'—which seems not to use the term inaugural year.

sentences.zh: 自無《大傳》，不得尋討。

translations.literal: Without the Great Tradition of my own, I could not pursue the inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Without the Great Tradition at hand I could not pursue the point.

sentences.zh: 一之與元，其事何別？

translations.literal: What difference is there between 'first' and 'inaugural'?
translations.idiomatic: What distinction is there between first and inaugural?

sentences.zh: 更有所見，幸請論之。

translations.literal: If you have further views, I hope you will discuss them.
translations.idiomatic: If you see further, please set it out.

sentences.zh: 」德林答曰：

translations.literal: Delin replied in answer:
translations.idiomatic: Delin replied:

sentences.zh: 攝之與相，其義一也。

translations.literal: Regency and assisting have the same meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Regency and assisting the throne mean the same thing.

sentences.zh: 故周公攝政，孔子曰「周公相成王」；

translations.literal: Thus the Duke of Zhou acted as regent, and Confucius said 'the Duke of Zhou assisted King Cheng';
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou as regent is what Confucius meant when he said the Duke of Zhou assisted King Cheng;

sentences.zh: 魏武相漢，曹植曰「如虞翼唐」。

translations.literal: Cao Cao assisted Han, and Cao Zhi said 'like Yu supporting Tang.'
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao assisting Han is what Cao Zhi meant by Yu supporting Tang.

sentences.zh: 或雲高祖身未居攝，灼然非理。

translations.literal: Some say Gaozu personally had not yet held the regency—this is plainly unreasonable.
translations.idiomatic: Some say Gaozu had not personally held the regency—that is plainly wrong.

sentences.zh: 攝者專賞罰之名，古今事殊，不可以體為斷。

translations.literal: Regency is the name for exclusive authority over rewards and punishments; affairs differ between ancient and modern times, and one cannot judge by outward form alone.
translations.idiomatic: Regency names the power to reward and punish alone; ancient and modern cases differ, and outward form cannot decide the matter.

sentences.zh: 陸機見舜肆類上帝，班瑞群後，便雲舜有天下，須格于文祖也，欲使晉之三主異於舜攝。

translations.literal: Lu Ji saw that Shun performed the suburban sacrifice to the Supreme Lord and distributed the jade regalia among the lords, and at once said Shun possessed All-under-Heaven and must present himself at the Temple of the Accomplished Ancestor—he wished to make the three rulers of Jin differ from Shun in regency.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji saw Shun sacrifice to Heaven and distribute jade to the lords and concluded Shun already held the realm and must visit the ancestral temple—he wanted Jin's three rulers to differ from Shun's regency.

sentences.zh: 竊以為舜若堯死，獄訟不歸，便是夏朝之益，何得不須格于文祖也？

translations.literal: I privately think that if, when Yao died, lawsuits did not return to Shun, he would have been Yi of the Xia dynasty—how could he not need to present himself at the Temple of the Accomplished Ancestor?
translations.idiomatic: If when Yao died lawsuits had not returned to Shun, he would have been Yi of Xia—why would he not still need the ancestral temple?

sentences.zh: 若使用王者之禮，便曰即真，則周公負扆朝諸侯，霍光行周公之事，皆真帝乎？

translations.literal: If using the rites of a king is taken to mean becoming true emperor, then the Duke of Zhou leaning on the screen while the feudal lords attended court, and Huo Guang performing the Duke of Zhou's affairs—were they all true emperors?
translations.idiomatic: If performing royal rites means becoming true emperor, then the Duke of Zhou receiving the lords behind the screen and Huo Guang acting as the Duke of Zhou did were both true emperors?

sentences.zh: 斯不然矣。

translations.literal: This is not so.
translations.idiomatic: That cannot be right.

sentences.zh: 必知高祖與舜攝不殊，不得從士衡之謬。

translations.literal: One must know that Gaozu's regency does not differ from Shun's, and one cannot follow Master Shi's error.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu's regency is no different from Shun's; one cannot follow Lu Ji's mistake.

sentences.zh: 或以為書元年者，當時實錄，非追書也。

translations.literal: Some think that writing the inaugural year means a contemporary true record, not a retroactive chronicle.
translations.idiomatic: Some hold that writing the inaugural year records events as they happened, not retroactively.

sentences.zh: 大齊之興，實由武帝，謙匿受命，豈直史也？

translations.literal: The rise of Great Qi was truly due to Emperor Wu; modestly concealing the receipt of the mandate—how could this be merely historiography?
translations.idiomatic: Great Qi rose through Emperor Wu; modestly hiding the receipt of the mandate is more than mere historiography.

sentences.zh: 比觀論者聞追舉受命之元，多有河漢，但言追數受命之歲，情或安之。

translations.literal: Comparing what I have seen, when discussants hear of retroactively raising the inaugural year of receiving the mandate, many are at a loss; but if one only speaks of retroactively counting the year of receiving the mandate, their feelings may perhaps be eased.
translations.idiomatic: Critics balk at retroactively dating the inaugural year of receiving the mandate, yet seem easier if one only counts back the year of receiving the mandate.

sentences.zh: 似所怖者元字耳，事類朝三，是許其一年，不許其元年也。

translations.literal: It seems what they fear is only the character yuan; the affair is like the morning-three [monkey fable]—they permit the one year but not the inaugural year.
translations.idiomatic: They seem to fear only the word inaugural—it is like the fable of morning three: they allow the first year but not the inaugural year.

sentences.zh: 案《易》「黃裳元吉」，鄭玄注雲：「如舜試天子，周公攝政。

translations.literal: Examining the Changes, 'yellow lower garment, inaugural auspiciousness,' Zheng Xuan's commentary says: 'like Shun testing as Son of Heaven, the Duke of Zhou acting as regent.'
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says 'yellow lower garment, inaugural auspiciousness'; Zheng Xuan glosses it: 'as when Shun tested as Son of Heaven, or the Duke of Zhou regented.'

sentences.zh: 」是以試攝不殊。

translations.literal: Thus testing and regency are not different.
translations.idiomatic: Testing the throne and regency are therefore the same.

sentences.zh: 《大傳》雖無元字，一之與元，無異義矣。

translations.literal: Though the Great Tradition lacks the character yuan, 'first' and 'inaugural' have no difference in meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Great Tradition lacks the word inaugural, first and inaugural mean the same.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》不言一年一月者，欲使人君體元以居正，蓋史之婉辭，非一與元別也。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn does not speak of 'one year' or 'one month' because it wishes rulers to embody the inaugural and dwell in rectitude—this is the historian's euphemistic wording; 'first' and 'inaugural' are not separate.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn avoids saying one year or one month so rulers may embody the inaugural and hold the center—it is the historian's euphemism, not a distinction between first and inaugural.

sentences.zh: 漢獻帝死，劉備自尊崇。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xian of Han died, Liu Bei elevated himself in self-esteem.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xian of Han died, Liu Bei proclaimed himself emperor.

sentences.zh: 陳壽蜀人，以魏為漢賊。

translations.literal: Chen Shou was a man of Shu and regarded Wei as the bandits of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shou, a native of Shu, treated Wei as usurpers against Han.

sentences.zh: 寧肯蜀主未立，已雲魏武受命乎？

translations.literal: How could he, before the lord of Shu was established, already say that Emperor Wu of Wei received the mandate?
translations.idiomatic: Would he date Cao Cao's receipt of the mandate before Liu Bei had even taken the throne?

sentences.zh: 士衡自尊本國，誠如高議，欲使三方鼎峙，同為霸名。

translations.literal: Master Shi esteemed his own state—truly as your lofty discussion says—wishing to make the three powers stand like a tripod, all bearing the name of hegemon.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji, as you rightly say, favored his own state and wanted the three realms to stand as rival hegemons.

sentences.zh: 習氏《漢晉春秋》，意在是也。

translations.literal: The Xi clan's Spring and Autumn of Han and Jin had this intent.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zuochi's Spring and Autumn of Han and Jin had the same aim.

sentences.zh: 至司馬炎兼併，許其帝號。

translations.literal: Only when Sima Yan annexed them did he grant their imperial titles.
translations.idiomatic: Only after Sima Yan's annexation did Jin recognize their imperial titles.

sentences.zh: 魏之君臣，吳人並以為戮賊，亦寧肯當塗之世，雲晉有受命之徵？

translations.literal: The rulers and ministers of Wei were all regarded by men of Wu as slaughtering bandits—how could they, in the age when Wei held the road, already say that Jin had signs of receiving the mandate?
translations.idiomatic: Wu treated Wei's rulers as murderous usurpers—would Wu chroniclers credit Jin's mandate while Wei still held power?

sentences.zh: 史者，編年也，故魯號《紀年》。

translations.literal: Historiography is annalistic chronology; hence Lu was styled Annals by Year.
translations.idiomatic: History is annalistic chronology—hence Lu's chronicle was called Annals by Year.

sentences.zh: 墨子又雲，吾見《百國春秋》。

translations.literal: Mozi also said: I have seen the Spring and Autumn of the Hundred States.
translations.idiomatic: Mozi too speaks of the Spring and Autumn of the Hundred States.

sentences.zh: 史又有無事而書年者，是重年驗也。

translations.literal: Histories also record years when nothing happened—this is to give weight to the verification of years.
translations.idiomatic: Histories sometimes record a year though nothing happened—because the year itself matters.

sentences.zh: 若欲高祖事事謙沖，即須號令皆推魏氏。

translations.literal: If one wishes Gaozu in every matter to be modest and restrained, then all orders must be attributed to the Wei clan.
translations.idiomatic: If Gaozu must appear humble in every act, every order must be credited to Wei.

sentences.zh: 便是編魏年，紀魏事，此即魏末功臣之傳，豈複皇朝帝紀者也。

translations.literal: That would be compiling Wei's years and recording Wei's affairs—this would be the biographies of Wei's late meritocrats, how could it still be the imperial annals of our dynasty?
translations.idiomatic: That would make the chronicle Wei's years and Wei's deeds—a biography of Wei's late ministers, not our dynasty's imperial annals.

sentences.zh: 陸機稱紀元立斷，或以正始，或以嘉平。

translations.literal: Lu Ji said the founding year and establishment of the break might be either Zhengshi or Jiaping.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji argued the founding year might begin at Zhengshi or at Jiaping.

sentences.zh: 束皙議雲，赤雀白魚之事。

translations.literal: Shu Xi's discussion spoke of the matters of the red sparrow and white fish.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Xi's argument cited the red sparrow and white fish portents.

sentences.zh: 恐晉朝之議，是並論受命之元，非止代終之斷也。

translations.literal: I fear the Jin court's discussion was jointly debating the inaugural year of receiving the mandate, not merely the break at dynastic end.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's debate likely concerned the inaugural year of receiving the mandate, not only the dynastic break.

sentences.zh: 公議雲陸機不議元者，是所未喻，願更思之。

translations.literal: The public discussion says Lu Ji did not debate the inaugural year—I do not understand this; I hope you will reconsider.
translations.idiomatic: Those who say Lu Ji never debated the inaugural year misunderstand him; please reconsider.

sentences.zh: 陸機以刊木著于《虞書》，龕黎見於商典，以蔽晉朝正始、嘉平之議，斯又謬矣。

translations.literal: Lu Ji used the felling of trees recorded in the Documents of Yu and the dark-haired people seen in the Shang canon to obscure the Jin court's Zhengshi and Jiaping discussions—this again is erroneous.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji cited Yu's felling of trees and the dark-haired people of Shang to cloud Jin's Zhengshi and Jiaping debate—another mistake.

sentences.zh: 唯可二代相涉，兩史並書，必不得以後朝創業之跡，斷入前史。

translations.literal: Only when two dynasties overlap may two histories be written together; one must never cut traces of a later dynasty's founding into an earlier history.
translations.idiomatic: Only overlapping dynasties may share a chronicle; a later dynasty's founding must never be inserted into an earlier history.

sentences.zh: 若然，則世宗、高祖皆天保以前，唯入魏氏列傳，不作齊朝帝紀，可乎？

translations.literal: If so, then Shizong and Gaozu, both before Tianbao, would enter only the Wei clan's biographies and not serve as imperial annals of the Qi dynasty—is that acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: By that logic Shizong and Gaozu, both before Tianbao, would appear only in Wei's biographies, not in Qi's imperial annals—is that acceptable?

sentences.zh: 此既不可，彼複何證！

translations.literal: Since this cannot be, what proof is there for that!
translations.idiomatic: If this cannot stand, what proof supports the other view?

sentences.zh: 是時中書侍郎杜台卿上《世祖武成皇帝頌》，齊主以為未盡善，令和士開以頌示德林。

translations.literal: At that time Secretariat Vice Director Du Taiqing submitted an Eulogy for Emperor Wucheng, the Shizu; the Qi ruler thought it not fully excellent and ordered He Shikai to show the eulogy to Delin.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat vice director Du Taiqing submitted an eulogy for Emperor Wucheng; the Qi ruler found it wanting and had He Shikai show it to Delin.

sentences.zh: 宣旨雲：「台卿此文，未當朕意。

translations.literal: An edict was proclaimed: "Taiqing's text does not suit Our mind."
translations.idiomatic: The edict ran: "Taiqing's piece does not suit Our mind."

sentences.zh: 以卿有大才，須敘盛德，即宜速作，急進本也。

translations.literal: Because you have great talent, you must narrate his splendid virtue; you should compose it at once and urgently present the draft.
translations.idiomatic: You have great talent—narrate his splendid virtue at once and submit the draft urgently."

sentences.zh: 」德林乃上頌十六章並序，文多不載。

translations.literal: Delin thereupon submitted an eulogy of sixteen sections with a preface; most of the text is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Delin submitted a sixteen-part eulogy with preface; most of the text is not preserved.

sentences.zh: 武成覽頌善之，賜名馬一匹。

translations.literal: Wucheng read the eulogy and approved it, bestowing one famous horse.
translations.idiomatic: Wucheng approved the eulogy and gave him a fine horse.

sentences.zh: 三年，祖孝徵入為侍中，尚書左僕射趙彥深出為兗州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year, Zu Xiaozheng entered as Palace Attendant, and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Zhao Yanshen went out as Governor of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Zu Xiaozheng became palace attendant and left vice director Zhao Yanshen left for Yanzhou as governor.

sentences.zh: 朝士有先為孝徵所待遇者，間德林，雲是彥深黨與，不可仍掌機密。

translations.literal: A court gentleman who had earlier been favored by Xiaozheng slandered Delin, saying he was Yanshen's partisan and could not continue to manage secrets.
translations.idiomatic: A courtier once favored by Xiaozheng whispered that Delin was Yanshen's partisan and must not keep handling secrets.

sentences.zh: 孝徵曰：「德林久滯絳衣，我常恨彥深待賢未足。

translations.literal: Xiaozheng said: "Delin long stagnated in crimson robes; I have often regretted that Yanshen did not treat the worthy sufficiently."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozheng said, "Delin long wore only low rank; I have often regretted Yanshen did not treat talent generously enough."

sentences.zh: 內省文翰，方以委之。

translations.literal: Reflecting within on literary matters, I am just about to entrust them to him.
translations.idiomatic: On reflection I am about to entrust literary affairs to him.

sentences.zh: 尋當有佳處分，不宜妄說。

translations.literal: Before long he will have a fine appointment; one should not speak rashly.
translations.idiomatic: He will soon receive a fine appointment—do not speak rashly."

sentences.zh: 」尋除中書侍郎，仍詔修國史。

translations.literal: Before long he was removed to Secretariat Vice Director and was further ordered to compile the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made secretariat vice director and ordered to compile the national history.

sentences.zh: 齊主留情文雅，召入文林館。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler cherished literary elegance and summoned him into the Forest of Literature Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi ruler, who loved letters, summoned him to the Forest of Literature.

sentences.zh: 又令與黃門侍郎顏之推二人同判文林館事。

translations.literal: He was further ordered together with Attendant of the Yellow Gate Yan Zhitui to jointly adjudicate affairs of the Forest of Literature Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He and attendant of the yellow gate Yan Zhitui were ordered to administer the hall together.

sentences.zh: 五年，敕令與黃門侍郎李孝貞、中書侍郎李若別掌宣傳。

translations.literal: In the fifth year an edict ordered him together with Attendant of the Yellow Gate Li Xiaozhen and Secretariat Vice Director Li Ruo to separately manage proclamation and transmission.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he, Li Xiaozhen, and Li Ruo were ordered to handle proclamations separately.

sentences.zh: 尋除通直散騎常侍，兼中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was removed to Vice Director of Attendants Cavalier Direct and Concurrent Secretariat Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made vice director of attendants cavalier direct, while retaining his secretariat post.

sentences.zh: 隆化中，假儀同三司。

translations.literal: During Longhua he was given provisional Three Excellencies of Equal Rank.
translations.idiomatic: During Longhua he was provisionally made equal to the three excellencies.

sentences.zh: 承光中，授儀同三司。

translations.literal: During Chengguang he was appointed Three Excellencies of Equal Rank.
translations.idiomatic: During Chengguang he received the rank in full.

sentences.zh: 及周武帝克齊，入鄴之日，敕小司馬唐道和就宅宣旨慰喻，雲：「平齊之利，唯在於爾。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou conquered Qi, on the day he entered Ye, he ordered Junior Major of the Horse Tang Dahe to go to his house and proclaim an edict of consolation, saying: "The profit of pacifying Qi lies solely in you."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou took Qi and entered Ye, he sent junior major Tang Dahe to Delin's home with words of reassurance: "The gain in pacifying Qi lies in you alone."

sentences.zh: 朕本畏爾逐齊王東走，今聞猶在，大以慰懷，宜即入相見。

translations.literal: We originally feared you would drive the King of Qi east in flight; now hearing you are still here, We are greatly comforted in mind—you should come in at once to meet Us.
translations.idiomatic: I feared you would flee east with the Qi king; learning you remain greatly comforts me—come at once to an audience."

sentences.zh: 」道和引之入內，遣內史字文昂訪問齊朝風俗政教、人物善惡，即留內省，三宿乃歸。

translations.literal: Dahe led him inside; the Inner Scribe Yuwen Ang was sent to inquire about Qi's customs, governance, teaching, and the good and bad among its men; he was detained in the inner secretariat and returned only after three nights.
translations.idiomatic: Dahe brought him in; inner scribe Yuwen Ang questioned him on Qi's customs, government, and leading figures; he stayed three nights in the inner secretariat before returning home.

sentences.zh: 仍遣從駕至長安，授內史上士。

translations.literal: He was further sent to follow the imperial carriage to Chang'an and was appointed Senior Scribe of the Inner Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the emperor to Chang'an and was made senior inner scribe.

sentences.zh: 自此以後，詔誥格式，及用山東人物，一以委之。

translations.literal: From this time forward, edict formats and the employment of men from east of the mountains were entirely entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter edict forms and the use of eastern talent were entirely in his hands.

sentences.zh: 武帝嘗于雲陽宮作鮮卑語謂群臣雲：「我常日唯聞李德林名，及見其與齊朝作詔書移檄，我正謂其是天上人。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu once at Yunyang Palace spoke in Xianbei to the assembled ministers: "I daily heard only the name Li Delin; when I saw him compose edicts and proclamations for the Qi court, I truly thought he was a man of heaven."
translations.idiomatic: At Yunyang Palace the emperor once addressed his ministers in Xianbei: "I had only heard Li Delin's name; when I saw the edicts and proclamations he wrote for Qi, I thought he must be a man from heaven."

sentences.zh: 豈言今日得其驅使，複為我作文書，極為大異。

translations.literal: Who would have said that today I could have him at my command, again writing documents for me—this is extremely strange.
translations.idiomatic: To have him at my command writing for me today is a marvel beyond words."

sentences.zh: 」神武公紇豆陵毅答曰：「臣聞明王聖主，得騏驎鳳凰為瑞，是聖德所感，非力能致之。

translations.literal: Duke Shenwu Hedouling Yi replied: "Your servant has heard that enlightened kings and sage rulers obtain qilin and phoenix as auspices—this is moved by sagely virtue, not something force can bring about."
translations.idiomatic: Duke Shenwu Hedouling Yi replied: "Sage rulers draw qilin and phoenix as portents through virtue, not by force."

sentences.zh: 瑞物雖來，不堪使用。

translations.literal: Though auspicious creatures come, they cannot be put to use.
translations.idiomatic: Such portents, though they appear, cannot be put to work.

sentences.zh: 如李德林來受驅策，亦陛下聖德感致，有大才用，無所不堪，勝於騏驎鳳凰遠矣。

translations.literal: As for Li Delin coming to receive driving and whipping, this too is brought about by Your Majesty's sagely virtue; he has great talent and use, nothing he cannot bear—far surpassing qilin and phoenix.
translations.idiomatic: Li Delin coming to serve is likewise your sagely virtue at work; his great talent can do anything—far better than qilin or phoenix."

sentences.zh: 」武帝大笑曰：「誠如公言。

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed greatly and said: "Truly as you say."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and said, "You are quite right."

sentences.zh: 」宣政末，授禦正下大夫。

translations.literal: At the end of Xuanzheng he was appointed Junior Grand Master of the Imperial Rectification.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Xuanzheng he was made junior grand master of imperial rectification.

sentences.zh: 大象初，賜爵成安縣男。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daxiang he was granted the noble rank of Baron of Chengan county.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Daxiang he was ennobled as baron of Chengan.

sentences.zh: 宣帝大漸，屬高祖初受顧命，邗國公楊惠謂德林曰：「朝廷賜令總文武事，經國任重，非群才輔佐，無以克成大業。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan was critically ill, as Gaozu had just received the dying charge, Duke of Hanguo Yang Hui said to Delin: "The court has granted you command of civil and military affairs; governing the state is a heavy charge—without a host of talents to assist, one cannot accomplish the great enterprise."
translations.idiomatic: As Emperor Xuan lay dying and Gaozu had just received the regency, Duke of Hanguo Yang Hui told Delin: "The court has put civil and military affairs in your hands; governing the state is too heavy for one man without able helpers."

sentences.zh: 今欲與公共事，必不得辭。

translations.literal: I now wish to undertake affairs together with you—you must not decline.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to work with you—you must not refuse."

sentences.zh: 」德林聞之甚喜，乃答雲：「德林雖庸芃，微誠亦有所在。

translations.literal: Delin heard this and was greatly pleased; he answered: "Though Delin is a mere common rush, some small sincerity is also present."
translations.idiomatic: Delin was delighted and answered: "Though I am only a common reed, I do have some small loyalty to offer."

sentences.zh: 若曲相提獎，必望以死奉公。

translations.literal: If you favor me with promotion, I surely hope to serve the public unto death.
translations.idiomatic: If you favor me, I hope to serve unto death."

sentences.zh: 」高祖大悅，即召與語。

translations.literal: Gaozu was greatly pleased and at once summoned him to converse.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was greatly pleased and summoned him at once.

sentences.zh: 劉昉、鄭譯初矯詔召高祖受顧命輔少主，總知內外兵馬事。

translations.literal: Liu Fang and Zheng Yi at first forged an edict summoning Gaozu to receive the dying charge to assist the young lord, with overall knowledge of internal and external military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang and Zheng Yi first forged an edict summoning Gaozu to the regency to assist the young emperor, with command of all armies.

sentences.zh: 諸衛既奉敕，並受高祖節度。

translations.literal: Once the guards received the edict, they all came under Gaozu's direction.
translations.idiomatic: The guard units, once the edict was issued, all fell under Gaozu's command.

sentences.zh: 鄭譯、劉昉議，欲授高祖塚宰，鄭譯自攝大司馬，劉昉又求小塚宰。

translations.literal: Zheng Yi and Liu Fang discussed wishing to grant Gaozu the office of Grand Minister, with Zheng Yi himself taking Grand Marshal and Liu Fang further seeking Junior Grand Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yi and Liu Fang planned to make Gaozu grand minister while Zheng Yi took grand marshal and Liu Fang sought junior grand minister.

sentences.zh: 高祖私問德林曰：「欲何以見處？

translations.literal: Gaozu privately asked Delin: "How do you wish to see me placed?"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu asked Delin privately, "How should I be placed?"

sentences.zh: 」德林雲：「即宜作大丞相，假黃鉞，都督內外諸軍事。

translations.literal: Delin said: "You should at once become Grand Chancellor, with provisional yellow battle-axe, directing all military affairs within and without."
translations.idiomatic: Delin said, "Make yourself grand chancellor at once, with the yellow battle-axe, commanding all armies within and without."

sentences.zh: 不爾，無以壓眾心。

translations.literal: Otherwise there is no means to suppress the hearts of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise you cannot hold the hearts of the multitude."

sentences.zh: 」及發喪，便即依此。

translations.literal: When the mourning was proclaimed, it was done immediately according to this.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning was proclaimed, he did exactly that.

sentences.zh: 以譯為相府長史，帶內史上大夫，昉但為丞相府司馬。

translations.literal: Zheng Yi was made Chancellor's Mansion Chief Clerk, carrying Senior Scribe of the Inner Secretariat; Liu Fang was only Chancellor's Mansion Major.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yi became the chancellor's chief clerk with senior inner scribe rank; Liu Fang received only the chancellor's major post.

sentences.zh: 譯、昉由是不平。

translations.literal: Zheng Yi and Liu Fang were thereby discontent.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yi and Liu Fang were displeased.

sentences.zh: 以德林為丞相府屬，加儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: Delin was made an aide of the Chancellor's Mansion, with additional Three Excellencies Equal to a Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Delin was made an aide in the chancellor's office with rank equal to a grand general.

sentences.zh: 未幾而三方構亂，指授兵略，皆與之參詳。

translations.literal: Before long the three regions raised disorder; in assigning military strategy he consulted Delin on all of it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the three regions rebelled; Gaozu consulted Delin on every military plan.

sentences.zh: 軍書羽檄，朝夕填委，一日之中，動逾百數。

translations.literal: Military documents and feathered proclamations piled up morning and evening; within a single day the movements exceeded a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Military dispatches piled up morning and night; in a single day he drafted more than a hundred.

sentences.zh: 或機速競發，口授數人，文意百端，不加治點。

translations.literal: Sometimes matters raced forth with urgency; he dictated to several men at once, the literary sense branching in a hundred directions, without adding polish or correction.
translations.idiomatic: When urgency pressed, he dictated to several scribes at once, intricate in sense, without a single revision.

sentences.zh: 鄖公韋孝寬為東道元帥，師次永橋，為沁水泛長，兵未得度。

translations.literal: Duke of Yun Wei Xiaokuan served as eastern-route commander-in-chief; the army halted at Yong Bridge, the Qin River having swollen long, and the troops could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Yun Wei Xiaokuan commanded the eastern army; halted at Yong Bridge by a swollen Qin River, his troops could not cross.

sentences.zh: 長史李詢上密啟雲：「大將梁士彥、宇文忻、崔弘度並受尉遲迥餉金，軍中慅慅，人情大異。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Li Xun submitted a secret memorial saying: "The great generals Liang Shiyan, Yuwen Xin, and Cui Hongdu all received gold gifts from Yuchi Jiong; in the army there is unrest and popular sentiment is greatly changed."
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Li Xun secretly reported: "Generals Liang Shiyan, Yuwen Xin, and Cui Hongdu have all taken gold from Yuchi Jiong; the army is unsettled and morale has shifted."

sentences.zh: 」高祖得詢啟，深以為憂，與鄭譯議，欲代此三人。

translations.literal: Gaozu received Xun's memorial and was deeply worried; he discussed with Zheng Yi and wished to replace these three men.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was deeply troubled and discussed with Zheng Yi replacing all three generals.

sentences.zh: 德林獨進計雲：「公與諸將，並是國家貴臣，未相伏馭，今以挾令之威，使得之耳。

translations.literal: Delin alone advanced a plan: "You and the generals are all eminent ministers of the state, not yet mutually submissive to one another; now only by the authority of holding the edict can you make them obey."
translations.idiomatic: Delin alone advised: "You and these generals are all eminent ministers who do not yet defer to one another; only the forged edict's authority holds them now."

sentences.zh: 安知後所遣者，能盡腹心，前所遣人，獨致乖異？

translations.literal: How does one know that those sent later can give full heart, while those sent before alone cause estrangement?
translations.idiomatic: How do you know replacements will prove loyal, while these three alone cause trouble?

sentences.zh: 又取金之事，虛實難明，即令換易，彼將懼罪，恐其逃逸，便須禁錮。

translations.literal: Moreover the matter of taking gold is hard to clarify as true or false; even if you replace them, they will fear guilt, perhaps flee, and you would have to imprison them.
translations.idiomatic: The gold charges are hard to prove; even if you replace them they may fear punishment, flee, and force you to imprison them.

sentences.zh: 然則鄖公以下，必有驚疑之意。

translations.literal: Then below the Duke of Yun there will surely be alarm and suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Then Wei Xiaokuan and those below him will surely grow alarmed and suspicious.

sentences.zh: 且臨敵代將，自古所難，樂毅所以辭燕，趙括以之敗趙。

translations.literal: Moreover replacing generals on the eve of battle has been difficult since antiquity—this is why Yue Yi left Yan, and Zhao Kuo thereby ruined Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Replacing generals on the eve of battle has always been perilous—Yue Yi left Yan for it, and Zhao Kuo ruined Zhao.

sentences.zh: 如愚所見，但遣公一腹心，明于智略，為諸將舊來所信服者，速至軍所，使觀其情偽。

translations.literal: As this foolish one sees it, send only one trusted man of yours, clear in strategy, whom the generals have long trusted, swiftly to the army camp to observe the truth and falsehood of the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Send one trusted man of yours, skilled in strategy and respected by the generals, swiftly to camp to observe the truth.

sentences.zh: 縱有異志，必不敢動。

translations.literal: Even if they have other intentions, they will surely not dare act.
translations.idiomatic: Even if they harbor other intentions, they will not dare act."

sentences.zh: 」丞相大悟曰：「若公不發此言，幾敗大事。

translations.literal: The Chancellor was greatly enlightened and said: "If you had not spoken these words, I would nearly have ruined the great affair."
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor exclaimed, "Without your words I would nearly have ruined everything."

sentences.zh: 」即令高熲馳驛往軍所，為諸將節度，竟成大功。

translations.literal: He at once ordered Gao Jiong to race by post relay to the army camp to direct the generals, and in the end a great achievement was accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Gao Jiong post-haste to take command of the generals, and the campaign succeeded.

sentences.zh: 凡厥謀謨，多此類也。

translations.literal: Generally his stratagems were mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his counsel was of this kind.

sentences.zh: 進授丞相府從事內郎。

translations.literal: He was advanced and appointed Chancellor's Mansion Attendant Inner Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to attendant inner gentleman in the chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 禪代之際，其相國總百揆、九錫殊禮詔策箋表璽書，皆德林之辭也。

translations.literal: At the time of the abdication and succession, the edicts, strategies, memorials, tables, and imperial seal documents for Chancellor Over All Affairs, Nine Bestowals, and special rites were all Delin's words.
translations.idiomatic: At the abdication, every edict for the chancellor's total authority, the nine bestowals, and the special rites was Delin's wording.

sentences.zh: 高祖登阼之日，授內史令。

translations.literal: On the day Gaozu ascended the throne he was appointed Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The day Gaozu took the throne he was made director of the palace secretariat.

sentences.zh: 初，將受禪，虞慶則勸高祖盡滅宇文氏，高熲、楊惠亦依違從之。

translations.literal: At first, when about to receive the abdication, Yu Qingze urged Gaozu to exterminate the Yuwen clan entirely; Gao Jiong and Yang Hui also wavered and followed.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was about to take the throne, Yu Qingze urged him to exterminate the Yuwen clan; Gao Jiong and Yang Hui wavered and agreed.

sentences.zh: 唯德林固爭，以為不可。

translations.literal: Only Delin firmly contended that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Only Delin argued firmly against it.

sentences.zh: 高祖作色怒雲：「君讀書人，不足平章此事。

translations.literal: Gaozu changed color in anger and said: "You are a man of books—not sufficient to deliberate on this matter."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu flushed with anger: "You are a scholar—not fit to judge this matter."

sentences.zh: 」於是遂盡誅之。

translations.literal: Thereupon they were all put to death.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuwen were slaughtered to the last.

sentences.zh: 自是品位不加，出於高、虞之下，唯依班例授上儀同，進爵為子。

translations.literal: From this time his rank was not increased; he fell below Gao and Yu, receiving only Senior Equal to the Three Excellencies by roster precedent, and advanced in noble rank to Viscount.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter his rank was not raised; he fell below Gao and Yu, receiving only senior equal to the three excellencies by precedent and advancement to viscount.

sentences.zh: 開皇元年，敕令與太尉任國公于翼、高熲等同修律令。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaihuang an edict ordered him together with Grand Marshal Duke of Renguo Yu Yi and Gao Jiong and others to jointly compile statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang 1 he was ordered with grand marshal Yu Yi of Renguo and Gao Jiong to revise the code.

sentences.zh: 事訖奏聞，別賜九環金帶一腰，駿馬一匹，賞損益之多也。

translations.literal: When the task was finished and reported, he was separately granted one nine-ring gold belt and one fine horse, rewarding how much he had added or subtracted.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was done he received a nine-ring gold belt and a fine horse, rewarding his many contributions.

sentences.zh: 格令班後，蘇威每欲改易事條。

translations.literal: After the administrative regulations and ordinances were promulgated, Su Wei often wished to change and alter articles.
translations.idiomatic: After the code was promulgated Su Wei often wanted to revise its articles.

sentences.zh: 德林以為格式已頒，義須畫一，縱令小有踳駁，非過蠹政害民者，不可數有改張。

translations.literal: Delin held that once formats were issued, meaning required uniformity; even if there were small contradictions, unless they exceeded corrupting government and harming the people, one could not repeatedly make changes.
translations.idiomatic: Delin held that once promulgated the code must stay uniform; minor inconsistencies that did not corrupt government or harm the people did not justify repeated revision.

sentences.zh: 威又奏置五百家鄉正，即令理民間辭訟。

translations.literal: Wei further memorialized to establish village heads for five hundred households, immediately entrusting them with civil lawsuits among the people.
translations.idiomatic: Wei also proposed village heads for five hundred households to judge local lawsuits.

sentences.zh: 德林以為本廢鄉官判事，為其裡閭親戚，剖斷不平，今令鄉正專治五百家，恐為害更甚。

translations.literal: Delin held that the original reason for abolishing village officials' judging of cases was that, being kin within lanes and hamlets, their judgments were unfair; now to have village heads exclusively govern five hundred households—he feared the harm would be even greater.
translations.idiomatic: Delin noted that village judges had been abolished because kinship made their rulings unfair; village heads over five hundred households might do even greater harm.

sentences.zh: 且今時吏部，總選人物，天下不過數百縣，于六七百萬戶內，詮簡數百縣令，猶不能稱其才，乃欲於一鄉之內，選一人能治五百家者，必恐難得。

translations.literal: Moreover the Ministry of Civil Service Affairs today oversees selection of personnel; All-under-Heaven has no more than several hundred counties—among six or seven million households, to select several hundred county magistrates still cannot match talent to post; yet one wishes within a single village to choose one man who can govern five hundred households—one must fear this will be hard to obtain.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel struggles to find capable magistrates for a few hundred counties among millions of households—how can one man per village govern five hundred households?

sentences.zh: 又即時要荒小縣，有不至五百家者，複不可令兩縣共管一鄉。

translations.literal: Moreover in remote border counties of the present day there are some with fewer than five hundred households; again one cannot have two counties jointly administer one village.
translations.idiomatic: Remote counties often have fewer than five hundred households; two counties cannot jointly administer one village.

sentences.zh: 敕令內外群官，就東宮會議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered civil and military officials of within and without to convene at the Eastern Palace for conference.
translations.idiomatic: An edict convened officials at the Eastern Palace for debate.

sentences.zh: 自皇太子以下，多從德林議。

translations.literal: From the Crown Prince downward, most followed Delin's discussion.
translations.idiomatic: From the crown prince down, most sided with Delin.

sentences.zh: 蘇威又言廢郡，德林語之雲：「修令時，公何不論廢郡為便？

translations.literal: Su Wei again spoke of abolishing commanderies; Delin said to him: "When compiling the ordinances, why did you not discuss abolishing commanderies as expedient?"
translations.idiomatic: Su Wei again proposed abolishing commanderies; Delin said to him, "When we compiled the code, why did you not argue then that abolishing commanderies would be expedient?"

sentences.zh: 今令才出，其可改乎！

translations.literal: The ordinances have only just been issued—how can they be changed!
translations.idiomatic: The code has barely been promulgated—surely it cannot be altered now!

sentences.zh: 」然高熲同威之議，稱德林狠戾，多所固勢。

translations.literal: " Yet Gao Jiong agreed with Wei's proposal, calling Delin harsh and obstinate, one who in many ways clung to entrenched power.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet Gao Jiong sided with Su Wei, denouncing Delin as fierce and unyielding and accusing him of defending entrenched interests at every turn.

sentences.zh: 由是高祖盡依威議。

translations.literal: Thereupon Gaozu fully followed Wei's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu therefore adopted Su Wei's position in full.

sentences.zh: 五年，敕令撰錄作相時文翰，勒成五卷，謂之《霸朝雜集》。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, by imperial order the documents written while serving as Chancellor were compiled and recorded, carved into five fascicles, and called the Miscellany of the Hegemon's Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Kaihuang, an edict ordered the compilation of Delin's writings from his years as chancellor into five fascicles titled the Miscellany of the Hegemon's Court.

sentences.zh: 序其事曰：

translations.literal: In prefacing the matter, he wrote:
translations.idiomatic: He prefaced the collection as follows:

sentences.zh: 竊以陽烏垂曜，微藿傾心，神龍騰舉，飛雲觸石。

translations.literal: I venture to observe: when the sun-bird casts down its radiance, the humble hollyhock inclines its heart; when the divine dragon rises aloft, flying clouds touch the stones.
translations.idiomatic: I take it that just as the sun draws even the humblest plant to face it, so a sage ruler draws all hearts toward him; just as a dragon's ascent stirs clouds from the very rocks, so a sovereign's rise stirs the world to respond.

sentences.zh: 聖人在上，幽顯冥符，故稱比屋可封，萬物斯睹。

translations.literal: When a sage is above, the hidden and the manifest are mysteriously aligned; hence it is said that every household could be enfeoffed, and all things witness it.
translations.idiomatic: When a sage ruler sits enthroned, the seen and unseen worlds fall into harmony—so it is said that every household merits enfeoffment and that all creation bears witness.

sentences.zh: 臣皇基草創，便豫驅馳，遂得參可封之民，為萬物之一，其為嘉慶，固以多也。

translations.literal: I, when the imperial foundation was first established, was already among those who rushed to serve; thus I became one of the people who could be enfeoffed, one among the myriad things—this joy is indeed great.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty was first being forged, I was already among those who hurried to its service; to count myself among the people worthy of enfeoffment, one creature in a transformed world—this fortune is immeasurably great.

sentences.zh: 若夫帝臣王佐，應運挺生，接踵於朝，諒有之矣。

translations.literal: As for ministers of emperors and assistants to kings, born in accord with the times and standing forth, following one another at court—surely this has happened.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers and kingmakers who rise to meet their age and fill the court one after another—such men have surely existed in every founding.

sentences.zh: 而班爾之妙，曲木變容，硃藍所染，素絲改色。

translations.literal: Yet the wonder of your excellences is that crooked wood changes its aspect, cinnabar and indigo dye it, and plain silk alters its color.
translations.idiomatic: Yet under such a ruler's transforming grace, bent timber takes new form, plain silk takes new color—men are remade as if by dye and craft.

sentences.zh: 二十二臣，功成盡美；

translations.literal: The twenty-two ministers— their merit complete and perfect;
translations.idiomatic: The twenty-two ministers of old achieved perfection in their service;

sentences.zh: 二十八將，效力于時。

translations.literal: the twenty-eight generals exerted their strength for the age.
translations.idiomatic: the twenty-eight generals gave their strength to their time.

sentences.zh: 種德積善，豈皆比於稷、契，計功稱伐，非悉類于耿、賈。

translations.literal: Those who planted virtue and accumulated goodness— were they all comparable to Hou Ji and Qi? Those who reckoned merit and claimed campaigns— were they all like Geng Yan and Jia Fu?
translations.idiomatic: Not every man who accumulates virtue equals a Hou Ji or a Qi; not every man who tallies victories matches a Geng Yan or a Jia Fu.

sentences.zh: 書契已還，立言立事，質非殆庶，何世無之。

translations.literal: Since the invention of writing, in establishing words and establishing deeds, the substance has rarely been nearly equal—what age lacks them?
translations.idiomatic: Since writing began, every age has produced men of word and deed—though few have ever come close to the greatest models.

sentences.zh: 蓋上稟睿後，旁資群傑，牧商鄙賤，屠釣幽微，化為侯王，皆由此也。

translations.literal: Generally, receiving wisdom above and assisted by heroes at the side—herders and merchants of humble birth, butchers and fishers in obscure places, transformed into marquis and king— all through this.
translations.idiomatic: It is because the ruler draws wisdom from above and talent from every quarter that herders, peddlers, butchers, and anglers in the deepest obscurity can rise to become lords and kings.

sentences.zh: 有教無類，童子羞于霸功；

translations.literal: Teaching without discrimination; the youth was ashamed of hegemonic achievements;
translations.idiomatic: When teaching knows no rank, even a youth may blush to speak of mere hegemony;

sentences.zh: 見德思齊，狂夫成於聖業。

translations.literal: seeing virtue and seeking to equal it, a madman accomplishes the sage's work.
translations.idiomatic: when men see virtue and strive to match it, even the reckless can be shaped to the sage's enterprise.

sentences.zh: 治世多士，亦因此焉。

translations.literal: An age of order has many scholars— also because of this.
translations.idiomatic: That is why an age of good government abounds in worthy men.

sentences.zh: 煙霧可依，騰蛇與蛟龍俱遠；

translations.literal: With mist and smoke to depend on, the soaring serpent goes as far as the flood dragon;
translations.idiomatic: Given mist and cloud to ride, even a flying serpent may travel as far as a dragon;

sentences.zh: 棲息有所，蒼蠅同騏驥之速。

translations.literal: with a place to rest, the fly matches the swiftness of a thoroughbred.
translations.idiomatic: given a place to alight, even a fly may keep pace with a thoroughbred.

sentences.zh: 因人成事，其功不難。

translations.literal: Relying on others to accomplish things— the achievement is not difficult.
translations.idiomatic: When one accomplishes things through the right men, great deeds are not hard to achieve.

sentences.zh: 自此而談，雖非上智，事受命之主，委質為臣，遇高世之才，連官接席，皆可以翊亮天地，流名鐘鼎，何必蒼頡造書，伊尹制命，公旦操筆，老聃為史，方可敘帝王之事，談人鬼之謀乎？

translations.literal: From this perspective, even if not of the highest intelligence, serving a ruler who receives the mandate, offering one's person as minister, meeting talents of a lofty age, holding office in succession and sharing the same mat— all may assist in illuminating Heaven and Earth and leave their names on bronze vessels. Why must one be Cangjie inventing writing, Yi Yin drafting commands, the Duke of Zhou wielding the brush, or Laozi serving as historiographer before one may narrate the affairs of emperors and kings and discuss the schemes of men and spirits?
translations.idiomatic: Seen in this light, even an ordinary man who serves a true Son of Heaven, pledges himself as a minister, and works beside the greatest talents of the age may help sustain the cosmos and win a name for the ages. Must one be Cangjie, Yi Yin, the Duke of Zhou, or Laozi before one may write of kings and speak of affairs beyond the human realm?

sentences.zh: 至若臣者，本慚賓實，非勳非德，廁軒冕之流，無學無才，處藝文之職。

translations.literal: As for one such as I, I am originally ashamed of being guest without substance, without merit or virtue, standing among the ranks of court robes, without learning or talent, occupying a literary post.
translations.idiomatic: As for me, I am a hollow ornament among the robed officials—without merit, without virtue, without learning or talent—yet placed in charge of literary affairs.

sentences.zh: 若不逢休運，非遇天恩，光大含弘，博約文禮，萬官百辟，才悉兼人，收拙裡閭，退仕鄉邑，不種東陵之瓜，豈過南陽之掾，安得出入閶闔之閫，趨走太微之庭，履天子之階，侍聖皇之側，樞機帷幄，沾及榮寵者也！

translations.literal: If I had not encountered a flourishing fortune, if I had not met heavenly favor— broad, bright, inclusive, and magnanimous, concise in culture and ritual, with myriad officials and hundred ministers all doubly talented—I would have gathered my clumsiness in lanes and hamlets, retired to serve in my native district, planted melons like the lord of Dongling, and perhaps not surpassed the clerk of Nanyang. How could I have passed in and out of the gates of Changhe, hurried through the court of Taiwei, trodden the Son of Heaven's steps, attended at the holy emperor's side, touched the inner secrets of state, and received glory and favor!
translations.idiomatic: Had I not met this golden age and its boundless grace—had every minister not been a man of doubled talent—I would have stayed in my village, grown melons like a commoner of Dongling, and counted myself lucky to be a petty clerk in Nanyang. How then could I have entered the imperial gates, hurried through the palace halls, climbed the Son of Heaven's steps, stood at the holy emperor's side, touched the inner councils of state, and tasted such honor?

sentences.zh: 昔歲木行將季，諒闇在辰，火運肇興，群官總己。

translations.literal: In years past the Wood phase was nearing its end; mourning obscurity lay in the chen position; the Fire fortune newly rose; all officials entrusted affairs to him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wood dynasty was nearing its end, the court sat in mourning, the Fire age was beginning, and every official entrusted power to our lord.

sentences.zh: 有周典八柄之所，大隋納百揆之日，兩朝文翰，臣兼掌之。

translations.literal: At the place where Zhou administered the Eight Handles, on the day Great Sui received the hundred officers, the literary documents of two dynasties—I held both in my charge.
translations.idiomatic: From the last days of Zhou's administration of the Eight Handles through the day Great Sui received the hundred officers, I held the literary records of two dynasties in my hands.

sentences.zh: 時溥天之下，三方構亂，軍國多務，朝夕填委。

translations.literal: At that time, under all Heaven, three regions were in rebellion; military and state affairs were many; morning and evening the desk was piled full.
translations.idiomatic: At that time rebellion flared in three directions across the realm, military and civil business multiplied, and every morning and evening the desk overflowed.

sentences.zh: 簿領紛紜，羽書交錯，或速均發弩，或事大滔天，或日有萬幾，或幾有萬事。

translations.literal: Ledgers were tangled, military dispatches crisscrossed—some urgent as releasing crossbows in unison, some matters vast enough to overflow Heaven; some days held ten thousand affairs, some affairs held ten thousand matters.
translations.idiomatic: Accounts piled up in confusion and urgent dispatches crossed in waves—some matters as pressing as a volley of crossbow bolts, some as vast as heaven itself; some days brought ten thousand decisions, and some decisions touched ten thousand things.

sentences.zh: 皇帝內明外順，經營區宇，吐無窮之術，運不測之神，幽贊兩儀，財成萬類。

translations.literal: The emperor was inwardly wise and outwardly compliant, managing the realm, issuing inexhaustible stratagems, deploying unfathomable spirit, secretly assisting the two principles and completing the myriad kinds.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was clear within and harmonious without, ordering the realm with inexhaustible strategy and unfathomable insight, quietly sustaining heaven and earth and shaping the myriad things.

sentences.zh: 諮謀台閣，曉喻公卿，訓率土之濱，責反常之賊。

translations.literal: He consulted and planned in the palace offices, instructed and explained to the high ministers, admonished those on the edges of the realm, and held accountable the rebellious traitors.
translations.idiomatic: He took counsel in the palace, instructed the chief ministers, taught the people to the farthest shore, and held rebels to account.

sentences.zh: 三軍奉律，戰勝攻取之方；

translations.literal: The three armies observed the law— methods for conquering in battle and taking by assault;
translations.idiomatic: The three armies obeyed his laws and learned the arts of victory and conquest;

sentences.zh: 萬國承風，安上治民之道。

translations.literal: the ten thousand states received the wind— the Way of securing superiors and governing the people.
translations.idiomatic: the myriad states caught his transforming influence and learned the way to secure rulers and govern the people.

sentences.zh: 讓受終之禮，報群臣之令，有憲章古昔者矣，有隨事作故者矣。

translations.literal: In the rites of yielding the end and responding to the orders of the assembled ministers, some followed ancient statutes and models, and some adapted to circumstances and created new precedents.
translations.idiomatic: In the rites of abdication and in edicts answering his ministers, some followed ancient precedent and some created new forms as events required.

sentences.zh: 千變萬化，譬彼懸河；

translations.literal: A thousand changes and ten thousand transformations— like a hanging river;
translations.idiomatic: His words shifted in endless forms, like a river in flood;

sentences.zh: 寸陰尺日，不棄光景。

translations.literal: Not an inch of shadow or a foot of daylight was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: not a moment of light or shadow was wasted.

sentences.zh: 大則天壤不遺，小則毫毛無失。

translations.literal: In great matters, heaven and earth were not overlooked; in small matters, not a hair was lost.
translations.idiomatic: In great affairs nothing under heaven escaped him; in small affairs not the slightest detail was missed.

sentences.zh: 遠尋三古，未聞者盡聞；

translations.literal: Searching far into the three antiquities, what had not been heard was all heard;
translations.idiomatic: Searching the three ancient ages, he recovered what had never been heard;

sentences.zh: 逖聽百王，未見者皆見。

translations.literal: listening distantly to the hundred kings, what had not been seen was all seen.
translations.idiomatic: listening across the hundred kings, he brought to light what had never been seen.

sentences.zh: 發言吐論，即成文章，臣染翰操牘，書記而已。

translations.literal: When he spoke and discoursed, it immediately became literature; I merely dipped the brush and held the tablet, recording—that was all.
translations.idiomatic: When he spoke, finished prose sprang forth; I only dipped my brush, held the writing board, and took down his words.

sentences.zh: 昔放勳之化，老人睹而未知；

translations.literal: In the past, under Fangxun's transforming influence, an old man saw it yet did not understand;
translations.idiomatic: In the age of Emperor Yao, an old man could witness the sage's transforming rule and still not comprehend it;

sentences.zh: 孔丘之言，弟子聞而不達。

translations.literal: Confucius's words— his disciples heard them yet did not penetrate them.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius's disciples could hear his teaching and still fail to grasp it.

sentences.zh: 愚情稟聖，多必乖舛。

translations.literal: My dull feelings receiving the sage— many must go awry.
translations.idiomatic: When a dull mind receives a sage's words, much must go wrong.

sentences.zh: 加以奏閣趨墀，盈懷滿袖，手披目閱，堆案積幾。

translations.literal: Added to this were presenting documents at the court and hurrying up the steps— filling bosom and sleeves, spreading them by hand and reading with the eye, heaping desk and piling writing table.
translations.idiomatic: On top of that came endless memorials at court, papers filling my sleeves and lap, documents spread before my eyes, piled high on desk and table.

sentences.zh: 心無別慮，筆不暫停，或畢景忘餐，或連宵不寐，以勤補拙，不遑自處。

translations.literal: My mind had no other thought; the brush did not pause for a moment. Sometimes I forgot meals until sunset; sometimes I went nights without sleep, using diligence to compensate for clumsiness, with no leisure to attend to myself.
translations.idiomatic: My mind held no other thought and my brush never stopped—sometimes I forgot to eat until sunset, sometimes I worked through the night, striving by sheer diligence to make up for my dullness, with no time left for myself.

sentences.zh: 其有詞理疏謬，遺漏闕疑，皆天旨訓誘，神筆改定。

translations.literal: Where wording and reasoning were loose or erroneous, where omissions and doubts remained, all were corrected by heaven's decree and the divine brush.
translations.idiomatic: Where my wording was loose, my reasoning flawed, or my text incomplete, the emperor's own hand revised and perfected it.

sentences.zh: 運籌建策，通幽達冥，從命者獲安，違命者悉禍。

translations.literal: In planning strategies and establishing policies, penetrating the hidden and reaching the obscure— those who followed commands obtained safety; those who defied commands all met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: His plans reached into the hidden depths of affairs: those who obeyed him found safety, and those who defied him met ruin.

sentences.zh: 懸測萬里，指期來事，常如目見，固乃神知。

translations.literal: Measuring ten thousand li afar, fixing dates for future events— it was always as if seen with the eye; truly it was divine knowledge.
