translations.idiomatic: He could measure events a thousand miles away and set dates for things yet to come as though he saw them with his own eyes—truly his knowledge was almost supernatural.

sentences.zh: 變大亂而致大平，易可誅而為淳粹，化成道洽，其在人文，盡出聖懷，用成典誥，並非臣意所能至此。

translations.literal: Transforming great disorder into great peace, changing what could be punished into pure simplicity— the transformation complete and the Way pervasive, its embodiment in human culture, all issued from the sage's breast and were used to form canonical edicts; this was not something my intent could reach.
translations.idiomatic: To turn great chaos into great peace, to transform a world of punishment into one of purity—this cultural transformation, these canonical edicts, all sprang from the sage emperor's mind and lay far beyond anything I could have conceived.

sentences.zh: 伯禹矢謨，成湯陳誓，漢光數行之劄，魏武《接要》之書，濟時拯物，無以加也。

translations.literal: Bo Yu's earnest counsel, Cheng Tang's declared oath, Han Guangwu's several edicts, and Cao Cao's book Jieyao—in saving the age and rescuing things, nothing can surpass these.
translations.idiomatic: Yu the Great's earnest counsel, King Tang's oath, Emperor Guangwu's edicts, and Cao Cao's Jieyao—nothing in history surpasses such writings for saving an age and rescuing the people, yet our emperor's words stand above even these.

sentences.zh: 屬神器大寶，將遷明德，天道人心，同謨歸往。

translations.literal: When the sacred vessel and great treasure were about to pass to enlightened virtue, the Way of Heaven and the hearts of men together voiced assent and turned toward him.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial regalia was about to pass to a ruler of enlightened virtue, Heaven and the people's hearts alike turned toward him in one accord.

sentences.zh: 周靜南面，每詔褒揚，在位諸公，各陳本志，璽書表奏，群情賜委。

translations.literal: With Zhou at peace and facing south, each edict praised and exalted; the ministers in office each declared their original intent; imperial letters, memorials, and petitions— the multitude's sentiments were entrusted and granted.
translations.idiomatic: As the Zhou court sat at peace and the emperor faced south, edict after edict praised his virtue; the ministers in office each declared their loyalty; imperial letters and memorials poured in, entrusting the will of the multitude to him.

sentences.zh: 臣寰海之內，忝曰一民，樂推之心，切于黎獻，欣然從命，輒不敢辭。

translations.literal: I, one man within the seas, humbly called one of the people—the heart of joyful endorsement pressing upon the common folk—I gladly accepted the command and dared not refuse.
translations.idiomatic: I, one man among all within the seas, counted myself fortunate even to be called one of the people; when the people's will pressed upon him, I gladly obeyed the command and did not dare refuse.

sentences.zh: 比夫潘勖之冊魏王，阮籍之勸晉後，道高前世，才謝往人，內手捫心，夙宵慚惕。

translations.literal: Compared with Pan Xu's enfeoffment of the King of Wei and Ruan Ji's urging of the Jin successor—the Way higher than former ages, yet talent inferior to men of the past—I press my hand to my heart, ashamed and fearful morning and night.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with Pan Xu's enfeoffment of the King of Wei or Ruan Ji's urging of the Jin successor, the cause was greater than any before, yet my talent fell far short of those earlier men; hand on heart, I felt shame and dread from dawn to dark.

sentences.zh: 檄書露板，及以諸文，有臣所作之，有臣潤色之。

translations.literal: Proclamations, open bulletins, and various writings— some I composed, some I polished.
translations.idiomatic: Among the proclamations, bulletins, and other documents, some I wrote myself and some I revised and polished.

sentences.zh: 唯是愚思，非奏定者，雖詞乖黼藻，而理歸霸德，文有可忽，事不可遺。

translations.literal: Only what was my own dull thought, not finalized by memorial— though the wording may depart from elegant ornament, the principle returns to the hegemon's virtue; the text may be overlooked, but the matter may not be discarded.
translations.idiomatic: What follows is only my own rough thinking, not text formally approved by memorial: though the language may fall short of court elegance, the substance belongs to the founding age; the style may be set aside, but the events must not be lost.

sentences.zh: 前奉敕旨，集納麓已還，至於受命文筆，當時制述，條目甚多，今日收撰，略為五卷雲爾。

translations.literal: Previously I received an imperial order to compile—from the gathering at the foundation onward, down to the writings of receiving the mandate; the compositions of that time were very numerous in their entries; today in collecting and compiling them, I have briefly made five fascicles— that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier I received an imperial order to compile everything from the first gathering of our rise down to the documents of receiving the mandate; the entries from that time were very numerous, and in compiling them today I have reduced them briefly to these five fascicles.

sentences.zh: 高祖省讀訖，明旦謂德林曰：「自古帝王之興，必有異人輔佐。

translations.literal: Gaozu finished reading it through, and the next morning said to Delin: "Since antiquity, whenever emperors and kings have risen, there have always been extraordinary men to assist them.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu had read it through, he said to Delin the next morning, "Since antiquity, every rise of an emperor has had an extraordinary man to assist him.

sentences.zh: 我昨讀《霸朝集》，方知感應之理。

translations.literal: Yesterday I read the Collection of the Hegemon's Court and only then understood the principle of mutual response.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday I read the Collection of the Hegemon's Court and at last understood how ruler and minister respond to one another.

sentences.zh: 昨宵恨夜長，不能早見公面。

translations.literal: Last night I regretted that the night was long and that I could not see your face sooner.
translations.idiomatic: Last night I cursed the long hours that kept me from meeting you sooner.

sentences.zh: 必令公貴與國始終。

translations.literal: I shall certainly see that you remain honored from the state's beginning to its end.
translations.idiomatic: I shall see that you remain honored from the founding of this dynasty to its end."

sentences.zh: 」於是追贈其父恆州刺史。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he posthumously enfeoffed Delin's father as Governor of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: With that he posthumously honored Delin's father as governor of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，上曰：「我本意欲深榮之。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor said: "My original intent was to honor him more deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor said, "My original intent was to honor him even more richly.

sentences.zh: 」複贈定州刺史、安平縣公，諡曰孝，以德林襲焉。

translations.literal: " He further posthumously enfeoffed him as Governor of Dingzhou and Duke of Anping County, with the posthumous title Filial, and Delin inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: " He then posthumously made Delin's father governor of Dingzhou and Duke of Anping, with the posthumous title Filial, and Delin inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 德林既少有才名，重以貴顯，凡制文章，動行於世。

translations.literal: Delin had already possessed a reputation for talent from youth, and now with added noble eminence, whatever compositions he made immediately circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Delin had been famous for talent since youth, and now with added rank and eminence, whatever he wrote at once circulated throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 或有不知者，謂為古人焉。

translations.literal: Some who did not know him took him for a man of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Some who did not know him assumed his writings were the work of an ancient master.

sentences.zh: 德林以梁士彥及元諧之徒頻有逆意，大江之南，抗衡上國。

translations.literal: Delin, because Liang Shiyan and men such as Yuan Xie repeatedly showed rebellious intent, and south of the Great River they contended against the superior state,
translations.idiomatic: Because Liang Shiyan, Yuan Xie, and their followers repeatedly showed rebellious intent and the lands south of the Yangzi still contended against the empire,

sentences.zh: 乃著《天命論》上之，其辭曰：

translations.literal: thereupon composed the Discourse on the Mandate of Heaven and presented it; its text says:
translations.idiomatic: Delin composed the Discourse on the Mandate of Heaven and submitted it. It reads:

sentences.zh: 粵若邃古，玄黃肇辟，帝王神器，歷數有歸。

translations.literal: In remote antiquity, when dark and yellow first opened forth, the sacred vessel of emperors and kings— the succession of fate had its destination.
translations.idiomatic: From deepest antiquity, when heaven and earth were first divided, the imperial regalia and the turn of dynastic fortune have always had their appointed destination.

sentences.zh: 生其德者天，應其時者命，確乎不變，非人力所能為也。

translations.literal: Heaven gives birth to the virtue; Fate matches the time— firm and unchanging, not something human power can accomplish.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven begets the virtue; fate answers the hour—this is fixed and unchanging, and no human force can alter it.

sentences.zh: 龍圖鳥篆，號諡遺跡，疑而難信，缺而未詳者，靡得而明焉。

translations.literal: Dragon charts, bird script, titles and posthumous names, traces left behind— what is doubtful and hard to believe, what is missing and not detailed, cannot all be made clear.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon charts, bird script, reign titles and posthumous names—much that survives is doubtful, fragmentary, or impossible to verify, and cannot all be made clear.

sentences.zh: 其在典文，煥乎緗素，欽明至德，莫盛于唐、虞，貽謀長世，莫過於文、武。

translations.literal: What is in the canonical writings shines upon the silk scrolls: reverent brilliance and supreme virtue— none surpasses Yao and Shun; legacy planning for long ages— none exceeds King Wen and King Wu.
translations.idiomatic: What survives in the canonical texts shines clear upon the page: in reverent brilliance and supreme virtue none surpass Yao and Shun; in planning for enduring rule none exceed King Wen and King Wu.

sentences.zh: 大隋神功積于文王，天命顯于唐叔。

translations.literal: Great Sui's divine merit accumulated in King Wen; the Mandate of Heaven was revealed in the Duke of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Great Sui's divine merit was accumulated in King Wen, and the Mandate of Heaven was revealed in the Duke of Tang.

sentences.zh: 昔邑姜方娠，夢帝謂己：「余命而子曰虞，將與之唐，而蕃育其子孫。

translations.literal: In the past, when Yi Jiang was pregnant, she dreamed that the Emperor said to her: "I name your son Yu, shall give him Tang, and shall nurture and multiply his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago, when Yi Jiang was pregnant, she dreamed that the Emperor said to her, "I name your son Yu, shall give him the state of Tang, and shall cause his descendants to flourish.

sentences.zh: 」及生，有文在其手曰「虞」，遂以命之。

translations.literal: " When he was born, there was writing on his hand saying "Yu," and so he was named accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: " When the child was born, the character Yu was written on his hand, and so he was given that name.

sentences.zh: 成王滅唐而封太叔。

translations.literal: King Cheng destroyed Tang and enfeoffed his younger uncle there.
translations.idiomatic: King Cheng destroyed the state of Tang and enfeoffed his younger uncle as its ruler.

sentences.zh: 又唐叔之封也，箕子曰：「其後必大。

translations.literal: Again, when the Duke of Tang was enfeoffed, Jizi said: "His descendants will surely become great.
translations.idiomatic: When the Duke of Tang received his fief, Jizi said, "His line will surely become great.

sentences.zh: 」《易》曰：「崇高富貴，莫大於帝王。

translations.literal: " The Book of Changes says: "Lofty eminence and rich nobility— nothing is greater than emperors and kings.
translations.idiomatic: " The Book of Changes says, "In loftiness, wealth, and nobility nothing surpasses the position of emperor and king.

sentences.zh: 」《老子》謂：「域內四大，王居一焉。

translations.literal: " Laozi says: "Within the realm there are four great things, and the king occupies one of them.
translations.idiomatic: " Laozi says, "Within the realm there are four great powers, and the king is one of them.

sentences.zh: 」此則名虞與唐，美兼二聖，將令其後必大，終致唐、虞之美，蕃育子孫，用享無窮之祚。

translations.literal: " Thus he was named Yu and Tang, combining the beauty of two sages, intending that his descendants would surely become great, ultimately attaining the beauty of Tang and Yu, multiplying descendants, and enjoying endless fortune.
translations.idiomatic: " Thus the names Yu and Tang joined the glory of two sage rulers, foretelling that his line would grow great, would ultimately attain the splendor of the eras of Tang and Yu, multiply its descendants, and enjoy boundless fortune.

sentences.zh: 逮皇家建國，初號大興，箕子必大之言，於茲乃驗。

translations.literal: When the imperial house established the state, its first name was Great Ascent— Jizi's words that "they will surely become great" were here verified.
translations.idiomatic: When our imperial house founded the state and first took the name Great Ascent, Jizi's prophecy that the line would become great was fulfilled at last.

sentences.zh: 天之眷命，懸屬聖朝，重耳區區，豈足雲也！

translations.literal: Heaven's favored mandate hangs upon the holy dynasty— Chong'er's petty case, how could it be worth mentioning!
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's favored mandate rests upon the holy dynasty—what are the petty fortunes of a Duke Wen of Jin compared with this!

sentences.zh: 有娀玄鳥，商以興焉；

translations.literal: You Song's dark bird— Shang rose thereby;
translations.idiomatic: You Song saw the dark bird, and Shang rose;

sentences.zh: 姜嫄巨跡，周以興焉；

translations.literal: Jiang Yuan's giant footprints— Zhou rose thereby;
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yuan saw the giant footprint, and Zhou rose;

sentences.zh: 邑姜夢帝，隋以興焉。

translations.literal: Yi Jiang dreamed of the Emperor— Sui rose thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Jiang dreamed of the Emperor, and Sui rose.

sentences.zh: 古今三代，靈命如一，本枝種德，奕葉丕基。

translations.literal: Ancient and modern, the three ages— the spiritual mandate is one; root and branch plant virtue, generation after generation establishing the great foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Past and present, the three sage dynasties share one pattern of heavenly mandate: root and branch alike plant virtue, and generation after generation lay a great foundation.

sentences.zh: 佐高帝而滅楚，立宣皇以定漢。

translations.literal: Assisting Gaodi to destroy Chu; establishing Emperor Xuan to stabilize Han.
translations.idiomatic: One ancestor helped Emperor Gaozu destroy Chu; another helped establish Emperor Xuan and stabilize Han.

sentences.zh: 東京太尉，關西孔子，生感遺鱣之集，歿降巨鳥之奇，累仁積善，大申休命。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal of the Eastern Capital, Confucius of Guanxi— at birth he was moved by the gathering of leftover fish; at death there descended the marvel of the giant bird; accumulating benevolence and gathering goodness, he greatly declared the mandate of rest.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Marshal of the Eastern Capital, the Confucius of Guanxi—at birth he was marked by the omen of returning fish, at death by the descent of a giant bird; through accumulated benevolence he greatly fulfilled Heaven's favor.

sentences.zh: 太祖挺生，庇民匡主，立殊勳于魏室，建盛業于周朝。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor stood forth, sheltering the people and supporting the ruler, establishing extraordinary merit in the Wei house and founding a flourishing enterprise in the Zhou dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor then arose to shelter the people and support his lord, winning extraordinary merit in Wei and building a great enterprise under Zhou.

sentences.zh: 啟翼軫之國，肇炎精之紀，爰受厥命，陟配彼天。

translations.literal: Opening the state under the Wings and Chariot asterisms, beginning the era of fire brilliance, then receiving that mandate and ascending to match Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the realm under the Wings and Chariot constellations, began the era of fire brilliance, received the mandate, and ascended to stand as Heaven's counterpart.

sentences.zh: 皇帝載誕之初，神光滿室，具興王之表，韞大聖之能。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the emperor's birth, divine light filled the room; he possessed the outward signs of a founding king and concealed within him the capacity of a great sage.
translations.idiomatic: At the emperor's birth divine light filled the chamber; he bore every outward sign of a founding king and concealed within him the power of a great sage.

sentences.zh: 或氣或雲，廕映於廊廟；

translations.literal: Whether qi or cloud, they shaded and reflected upon the halls and temples;
translations.idiomatic: Whether as breath or cloud, his presence cast its shade over the palace halls;

sentences.zh: 如天如日，臨照於軒冕。

translations.literal: like Heaven, like the sun, overlooking and illuminating the court robes.
translations.idiomatic: like heaven, like the sun, he looked down upon the court.

sentences.zh: 內明外順，自險獲安，豈非萬福扶持，百祿攸集。

translations.literal: Inwardly clear and outwardly compliant, from danger he obtained safety— was this not the support of ten thousand blessings and the gathering of a hundred emoluments?
translations.idiomatic: Clear within and harmonious without, he found safety even in peril—was this not the support of every blessing and the gathering of every fortune?

sentences.zh: 有周之末，朝野騷然，降志執均，鎮衛宗社。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhou, court and countryside were in turmoil; he lowered his ambition and held the balance, guarding and protecting the imperial altars.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Northern Zhou, when court and countryside were in turmoil, he humbled his ambition, held the scales of power even, and guarded the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 明神饗其德，上帝付其民，誅奸逆於九重，行神化于四海。

translations.literal: Bright spirits enjoyed his virtue; High God entrusted the people to him; he executed traitors and rebels within the ninefold palace and practiced divine transformation throughout the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Bright spirits delighted in his virtue, and High God entrusted the people to him; he executed traitors within the palace and spread his transforming rule across the four seas.

sentences.zh: 于斯時也，尉迥據有齊累世之都，乘新國易亂之俗，驅馳蛇豕，連合縱橫，地乃九州陷三，民則十分擁六。

translations.literal: At that time Wei Chixiong held the capital of Qi accumulated over generations, riding the customs of a new state prone to disorder; driving serpents and swine, he joined alliances north and south; of the land, three of the nine provinces fell; of the people, six of ten parts rallied to him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wei Chixiong held the ancient capital of Qi, exploited the disorder of a newly founded state, rallied barbarian allies, and wove a web of alliances—three of the nine provinces and six tenths of the people were in his grasp.

sentences.zh: 王謙乘連率之威，憑全蜀之險，興兵舉眾，震盪江山，鴆毒巴、庸，蠶食秦、楚。

translations.literal: Wang Qian relied on the authority of a regional commander, depended on the full defenses of Shu, raised troops and gathered masses, shaking rivers and mountains; he poisoned Ba and Yong and nibbled away at Qin and Chu like silkworms eating mulberry.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qian wielded the power of a military governor, relied on the natural defenses of all Shu, raised armies that shook the land, poisoned Ba and Yong, and gnawed away at Qin and Chu.

sentences.zh: 此二虜也，窮凶極逆，非欲割鴻溝之地，閉劍閣之門，皆將長戟強弩，睥睨宸極。

translations.literal: These two foes, utterly vicious and utterly rebellious— it was not that they wished merely to carve out the land of Honggou or shut the gates of Sword Pass; all intended with long halberds and strong crossbows to look down upon the imperial pole.
translations.idiomatic: These two rebels were utterly vicious and utterly defiant: they did not merely seek to hold the Hong Canal or close the gates of Sword Pass—they meant to train long halberds and strong crossbows upon the imperial throne itself.

sentences.zh: 從漳河而達負海，連岱岳而距華陽，迫脅荊蠻，吐納江漢。

translations.literal: From the Zhang River reaching to the eastern sea, connecting Mount Tai and facing Huayang, pressing and coercing the Jing barbarians, exhaling and inhaling the Yangzi and Han.
translations.idiomatic: From the Zhang River to the eastern sea, from Mount Tai to Huayang, they pressed upon the southern tribes and sought to command the Yangzi and Han.

sentences.zh: 佐鬥嫁禍，紛若蝟毛；

translations.literal: Aiding one side in a fight and shifting disaster onto others— tangled like hedgehog quills;
translations.idiomatic: They stirred others to fight and shifted disaster onto rivals, tangled as thick as hedgehog quills;

sentences.zh: 曝骨履腸，間不容礪。

translations.literal: Bones were exposed and entrails trodden underfoot; not even the width of a whetstone could fit between.
translations.idiomatic: Corpses lay so thick that bones were exposed and entrails trampled underfoot—not even a whetstone could be slipped between them.

sentences.zh: 爾乃奉殪戎之命，運先天之略，不出戶庭，推轂分閫，一麾以定三方，數旬而清萬國。

translations.literal: Then he received the mandate to destroy the foe, employed the strategy of Antecedent Heaven, without leaving the courtyard gate pushed the chariot wheel and divided command— with one wave of the banner he settled the three regions, and in several tens of days cleared all the states.
translations.idiomatic: Then he took up Heaven's command to crush the enemy, wielded the strategy ordained before creation, and without leaving his own gate pushed generals forward and divided command: one signal settled the three regions, and within weeks the myriad states were pacified.

sentences.zh: 蕩滌天壤之速，規摹指畫之神，造化以來，弗之聞也。

translations.literal: The speed with which heaven and earth were swept clean, the divinity of his planning and directing— since creation, none has heard of the like.
translations.idiomatic: The speed with which he swept heaven and earth clean, the godlike precision of his design—since the world began, nothing like it had ever been heard of.

sentences.zh: 光熙前緒，罔有不服，煙雲改色，鐘石變音，三靈顧望，萬物影響。

translations.literal: He brightened and extended the former lineage; none failed to submit. Cloud and mist changed color, bells and stones changed tone; the Three Spirits looked back in hope, and the ten thousand things responded like shadows.
translations.idiomatic: He restored and enlarged the imperial line, and none remained unsubmissive. Clouds changed hue, bells and chimes altered their tone; heaven, earth, and the spirits turned to look upon him, and the myriad things answered as shadows answer light.

sentences.zh: 木運告盡，褰裳克讓，天曆在躬，推而弗有。

translations.literal: The Wooden Cycle announced its end; he could have lifted his robes and yielded. The heavenly calendar was upon his person, yet he pushed it away and would not possess it.
translations.idiomatic: When the age of wood had run its course, he was able to step aside and yield; though the heavenly mandate rested upon him, he thrust it away and refused to take it.

sentences.zh: 百辟庶尹，四方嶽牧，稽圖讖之文，順億兆之請，披肝瀝膽，晝歌夜吟，方屈箕潁之高，式允幽明之願。

translations.literal: The hundred ministers and myriad officials, the frontier governors of the four directions, consulted texts of charts and prognostications and followed the petitions of a hundred million; laying bare liver and pouring out gall, singing by day and chanting by night, they at last bent the lofty heights of Ji and Ying and thereby fulfilled the wishes of the living and the dead.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers and frontier governors consulted portents and charts and bowed to the pleas of the masses; with utter sincerity they sang his praises day and night until even the lofty recluses of Ji and Ying were moved, and the wishes of both worlds were fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 基命宥密，如恆如升，推帝居歆，創業垂統。

translations.literal: He founded the mandate in deep secrecy, constant as enduring, rising as ascending; he extended the imperial seat and received delight, founding the enterprise and handing down the succession.
translations.idiomatic: He laid the foundation of the mandate in quiet depth, steady and ever rising; he enlarged the throne and won Heaven's favor, founding the dynasty and bequeathing its succession.

sentences.zh: 殊徽號，改服色，建都邑，敘彝倫，薄賦輕徭，慎刑恤獄，除繁苛之政，興清靜之風，去無用之官，省相監之職。

translations.literal: He distinguished regnal titles, changed ceremonial colors, established capitals, ordered the constant virtues, lightened taxes and reduced corvée, exercised care in punishment and compassion in prisons, removed burdensome harsh policies, raised the breeze of purity and stillness, eliminated useless offices, and reduced overlapping supervisory posts.
translations.idiomatic: He set apart his reign title, changed ceremonial colors, established the capital, and put the moral order in sequence; he lightened taxes and corvée, tempered punishments and showed mercy in the prisons, swept away oppressive laws, fostered a spirit of quiet governance, abolished useless offices, and cut redundant supervisory posts.

sentences.zh: 奇才間出，盛德無隱，星精雲氣，共趨走於階墀，山神海靈，咸燮理於台閣。

translations.literal: Outstanding talents appeared one after another; magnificent virtue hid nothing. Star essences and cloud qi all hastened to the palace steps; mountain spirits and sea numina all assisted in governance at the terrace halls.
translations.idiomatic: Men of extraordinary talent emerged in succession, and his great virtue concealed nothing; star-spirits and auspicious clouds gathered at his palace steps, and mountain and sea spirits alike lent their aid in the halls of state.

sentences.zh: 東漸日穀，西被月川，教暨北溟之表，聲加南海之外。

translations.literal: East he reached to Rigu, west he covered Yuechuan; his teaching extended beyond the northern sea, his renown added beyond the southern sea.
translations.idiomatic: His influence spread east to the Valley of the Sun and west to the River of the Moon; his teachings reached beyond the northern sea, and his fame resounded past the southern sea.

sentences.zh: 悠悠沙漠，區域萬里，蠢蠢百蠻，莫之與競。

translations.literal: Vast deserts stretched for ten thousand li; countless barbarian peoples— none could compete with him.
translations.idiomatic: Across boundless deserts ten thousand li wide, amid countless barbarian tribes, none could rival him.

sentences.zh: 五帝所不化，三王所未賓，屈膝頓顙，盡為臣妾。

translations.literal: Those the Five Emperors could not transform, those the Three Kings had never received as guests— all bent knee and bowed forehead and became subjects and servants.
translations.idiomatic: Peoples whom the Five Emperors had failed to transform and the Three Kings had never brought to court all bent the knee and bowed the head, becoming his subjects and servants.

sentences.zh: 殊方異類，書契不傳，梯山越海，貢琛奉贄，欣欣如也。

translations.literal: Distant regions and alien kinds, untransmitted in written records, climbed mountains and crossed seas, presenting tribute and offering gifts, all joyful and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Strange lands and foreign peoples never named in any record climbed mountains and crossed seas to bring tribute and gifts, rejoicing as they came.

sentences.zh: 巢居穴處，化以宮室；

translations.literal: Those who dwelled in nests and caves were transformed with palaces and chambers;
translations.idiomatic: People who had lived in nests and caves were taught to dwell in halls and chambers;

sentences.zh: 不火不粒，訓以庖廚。

translations.literal: Those who did not use fire or grain were instructed with kitchens and stoves.
translations.idiomatic: those who neither cooked with fire nor ate grain were taught the ways of hearth and kitchen.

sentences.zh: 禮樂合天地之同，律呂節寒暑之候，製作詳垂衣之後，淳粹得神農之前。

translations.literal: Rites and music harmonized with the unity of heaven and earth; pitch pipes regulated the seasons of cold and heat. Institutions were more detailed than after the rule of draped garments, and purity was attained such as before Shennong.
translations.idiomatic: Rites and music matched the harmony of heaven and earth; pitch pipes measured the turning of the seasons. His institutions surpassed even the age of effortless rule, and their purity recalled the world before Shennong.

sentences.zh: 遨遊文雅之場，出入杳冥之極，合神謨鬼，通幽洞微。

translations.literal: He roamed the arena of refined letters, entered and exited the utmost reaches of the obscure dark, harmonized with divine plans and ghostly wisdom, and penetrated the hidden and discerned the subtle.
translations.idiomatic: He moved freely in the realm of letters, passed in and out of the deepest mysteries, aligned himself with spirits and ghosts, and penetrated what is hidden and subtle.

sentences.zh: 群物歲成，含生日用，飲和氣以自得，沐玄澤而不知也。

translations.literal: The myriad things ripened each year and contained life for daily use; they drank harmonious qi and found self-contentment, bathed in dark grace without knowing it.
translations.idiomatic: The myriad creatures flourished year by year and lived out their days; they drank the air of harmony and rested content, bathed in his deep beneficence without even knowing it.

sentences.zh: 丹雀為使，玄龜載書，甘露自天，醴泉出地。

translations.literal: The crimson sparrow served as messenger; the dark tortoise bore the script. Sweet dew came from heaven, and sacrificial spring issued from the earth.
translations.idiomatic: The crimson sparrow came as Heaven's messenger, the dark tortoise bore the sacred text; sweet dew descended from the sky, and sacrificial springs welled up from the ground.

sentences.zh: 神禽異獸，珍木奇草，望風觀海，應化歸風。

translations.literal: Divine birds and rare beasts, precious trees and strange plants— facing the wind and observing the sea, responding to transformation and returning with the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Divine birds and exotic beasts, rare trees and wondrous plants—all turned toward his wind and watched his tide, answering his transforming rule and gathering to his banner.

sentences.zh: 備休祥於圖牒，罄幽遐而戾止。

translations.literal: Auspicious signs were complete in charts and records; the remotest depths all came and settled.
translations.idiomatic: Every auspicious omen was recorded in the annals, and even the farthest corners of the earth came to dwell in peace under him.

sentences.zh: 猶且父天子民，兢兢翼翼，至矣大矣，七十四帝，曷可同年而語哉！

translations.literal: Still further he was father to heaven and child to the people, cautious and reverent— sublime, grand! Of the seventy-four emperors, how could any be spoken of in the same breath!
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was still Heaven's son and the people's father, careful and reverent in all things—how sublime, how vast! Of the seventy-four emperors of history, which could be mentioned in the same breath as he?

sentences.zh: 若夫天下之重，不可妄據，故唐之許由，夏之伯益，懷道立事，人授而弗可也。

translations.literal: As for the weight of all under heaven, it cannot be rashly seized. Hence Tang's Xu You and Xia's Bo Yi, holding the Way and establishing affairs— when men would grant it, they could not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The weight of the realm cannot be seized lightly. That is why Xu You of Tang and Bo Yi of Xia, though they possessed the Way and stood ready to serve, refused the throne even when men would have given it to them.

sentences.zh: 軒初四帝，周余六王，藉世因基，自取而不得也。

translations.literal: The four emperors at the beginning of Xuanyuan, the six kings remaining in Zhou— relying on generations and inheriting foundations, even when taking for themselves they could not obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: The four emperors at the founding of Xuanyuan's line, the six kings who survived in Zhou—though they inherited power across generations, even when they seized it for themselves they could not keep the realm.

sentences.zh: 孟軻稱仲尼之德過於堯、舜，著述成帝者之事，弟子備王佐之才，黑不代蒼，泣麟歎鳳，棲棲汲汲，雖聖達而莫許也。

translations.literal: Mencius said Confucius's virtue surpassed Yao and Shun; he wrote works completing the affairs of emperors, and his disciples possessed the talent of kings' assistants. Black does not replace blue; he wept at the qilin and sighed at the phoenix, restless and urgent— though sage and accomplished, none granted him the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Mencius declared that Confucius's virtue exceeded that of Yao and Shun; his writings completed the work of emperors, and his disciples had the talent to assist kings. Yet blue is not replaced by black: he wept when the qilin appeared and sighed at the phoenix's flight, restless and striving—though a sage, no one would grant him the throne.

sentences.zh: 蚩尤則黃帝抗衡，共工則黑帝勍敵，項羽誅秦摧漢，宰割神州，角逐爭驅，盡威力而無就也。

translations.literal: Chiyou matched the Yellow Emperor as a rival; Gonggong was the Black Emperor's fierce foe. Xiang Yu destroyed Qin and crushed Han, carved up the divine land, raced and competed in pursuit, exerting all his force yet achieving nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Chiyou stood as the Yellow Emperor's equal; Gonggong was a formidable enemy of the Black Emperor. Xiang Yu overthrew Qin and battered Han, carved up the heartland, and raced rivals for supremacy—yet for all his power he achieved nothing.

sentences.zh: 其餘欻起妖妄，曾何足數！

translations.literal: The rest who suddenly rose in demonic delusion— how could they be worth counting!
translations.idiomatic: As for the others who sprang up in demonic madness, they are scarcely worth mentioning!

sentences.zh: 賊子逆臣，所以為亂，皆由不識天道，不悟人謀，牽逐鹿之邪說，謂飛鳧而為鼎。

translations.literal: Traitorous sons and rebellious ministers— what made their turmoil was all from not knowing Heaven's Way, not comprehending human schemes, clinging to the perverse doctrine of chasing the deer, and thinking a flying wild duck could become the cauldron.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellious sons and treacherous ministers bring chaos because they do not know Heaven's Way or understand human design; they cling to the false doctrine of chasing the deer and imagine that a wild duck in flight can become the imperial cauldron.

sentences.zh: 若使四凶爭八元之誠，三監同九臣之志，韓信、彭越深明帝子之符，孫述、隗囂妙識真人之出，尉迥同謳歌之類，王謙比獄訟之民，福祿蟬聯，胡可窮也！

translations.literal: If the Four Evils had vied with the sincerity of the Eight Worthies, the Three Supervisors shared the resolve of the Nine Ministers, Han Xin and Peng Yue deeply understood the signs of the Son of Heaven, Sun Shu and Wei Xiao finely recognized the emergence of the true man, Wei Chixiong resembled those who sang praises, and Wang Qian compared to people settling lawsuits— blessings and emoluments would have linked like cicada shells; how could they be exhausted!
translations.idiomatic: Had the Four Evils competed in virtue with the Eight Worthies, had the Three Supervisors shared the loyalty of the Nine Ministers, had Han Xin and Peng Yue truly read the signs of Heaven's chosen son, had Sun Shu and Wei Xiao discerned the rise of the true ruler, had Wei Chixiong joined the chorus of praise and Wang Qian been like a people at peace in court—then blessings and honors would have flowed without end!

sentences.zh: 而違天逆物，獲罪人神。

translations.literal: Yet they defied Heaven and went against things, and found guilt before men and spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Instead they defied Heaven and turned against the natural order, and so earned condemnation from both men and spirits.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 此前事之大戒矣。

translations.literal: This is the great warning of prior affairs.
translations.idiomatic: This is the great lesson of times past.

sentences.zh: 誅夷烹醢，歷代共尤，僭逆凶邪，時煩獄吏，其可不戒慎哉！

translations.literal: Execution, extermination, boiling and mincing— generations share these abominations; usurping, rebellious, vicious and wicked men at times trouble the prison clerks. How could one not be vigilant and cautious!
translations.idiomatic: Slaughter, extermination, boiling and dismemberment—these horrors repeat in every age; usurpers and wicked rebels keep the prison officers busy. How can one fail to take warning!

sentences.zh: 蓋積惡既成，心自絕於善道，物類相感，理必至於誅戮。

translations.literal: For once accumulated evil is formed, the heart itself cuts off from the path of goodness; things of a kind respond to each other— principle necessarily leads to execution.
translations.idiomatic: When evil accumulates to the full, the heart severs itself from the path of goodness; like calls to like, and by natural law punishment must follow.

sentences.zh: 天奪其魄，鬼惡其盈故也。

translations.literal: Heaven stripped away their souls; ghosts hated their fullness— such was the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven took their souls, and ghosts loathed their excess—that is why it was so.

sentences.zh: 大帝聰明，群臣正直，耳目濫於率土，賞罰參于國朝，輔助一人，覆育兆庶。

translations.literal: The great emperor is wise and clear; ministers are upright. Eyes and ears overflow across all the land; reward and punishment participate in the state court, assisting the one man and covering and nurturing the hundred millions.
translations.idiomatic: The great emperor is wise and discerning, his ministers upright; his eyes and ears reach every corner of the realm, his rewards and punishments issue from the court. They assist the one ruler and shelter and nurture the countless people.

sentences.zh: 豈有食人之祿，受人之榮，包藏禍心而不殲盡者也？

translations.literal: How could there be those who eat men's salaries, receive men's honors, conceal treacherous hearts, and not be utterly destroyed?
translations.idiomatic: Can anyone eat the state's salary, accept its honors, hide treacherous intent, and not be utterly destroyed?

sentences.zh: 必當執法未處其罪，司命已除其籍。

translations.literal: Surely when the law had not yet punished their crime, the Director of Fates had already struck their names from the register.
translations.idiomatic: Even before the law could pronounce sentence, the Director of Fates had already struck their names from the book of life.

sentences.zh: 自古明哲，慮遠防微，執一心，持一德，立功坐樹，上書削槁，位尊而心逾下，祿厚而志彌約，寵盛思之以懼，道高守之以恭，克念於此，則奸回不至。

translations.literal: Since antiquity the wise and clear have thought far and guarded against the subtle, held one heart and maintained one virtue; achieved merit yet sat beneath a tree, submitted memorials yet burned the drafts; rank high yet heart more humble, salary thick yet ambition more restrained; favor abundant yet thought of with fear, Way lofty yet guarded with reverence. If one can reflect on this, then treachery and perversity will not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity the wise have looked far ahead and guarded against small beginnings, kept one heart and one virtue; they earned merit yet sat beneath a tree, wrote memorials yet burned the drafts; though high in rank their hearts grew humbler, though richly paid their ambitions grew simpler; in favor they felt fear, in virtue they kept reverence. Hold fast to this, and treachery will never come near.

sentences.zh: 事乃畏天，豈惟愛禮，謙光滿覆，義在知幾，吉凶由人，妖不自作。

translations.literal: Affairs require fearing Heaven— not merely loving ritual. Modest light fills and covers; righteousness lies in knowing the subtle signs. Fortune and calamity depend on men; portents do not arise of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In public life one must fear Heaven—not merely honor ritual. Humility fills and protects; righteousness lies in reading the first signs. Fortune and disaster come from men; evil omens do not arise on their own.

sentences.zh: 眾星共極，在天成象。

translations.literal: The myriad stars share one pole— in heaven they form the pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The myriad stars revolve around one pole—in heaven this is the pattern of order.

sentences.zh: 夙沙則主雖愚蔽，民盡知歸；

translations.literal: In Suosha, though the lord was foolish and blind, the people all knew where to turn;
translations.idiomatic: In Suosha, though the ruler was foolish and benighted, the people all knew whom to follow;

sentences.zh: 有苗則始為跋扈，終而大服。

translations.literal: Youmiao at first was overbearing, but in the end greatly submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Youmiao at first was arrogant and defiant, but in the end submitted fully.

sentences.zh: 漢南諸國，見一面以從殷；

translations.literal: The states south of the Han, seeing one face, submitted to Yin;
translations.idiomatic: The states south of the Han, upon a single audience, submitted to Yin;

sentences.zh: 河西將軍，率五郡以歸漢。

translations.literal: The general of Hexi led five commanderies to return to Han.
translations.idiomatic: the general of Hexi led five commanderies back to Han.

sentences.zh: 故能招信順之助，保太山之安。

translations.literal: Thus they could summon the aid of the trusting and compliant and preserve the security of Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Thus they won the support of the willing and kept their dominion secure as Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 彼陳國者，盜竊江外，民少一郡，地減半州，遇受命之主，逢太平之日，自可獻土銜璧，乞同溥天。

translations.literal: That state of Chen, having stolen territory south of the river, with population less than one commandery and land less than half a province— encountering a ruler who received the Mandate and meeting days of great peace— naturally could have surrendered territory bearing jade disks and begged to share the breadth of heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Chen had seized land south of the Yangzi, with fewer people than a single commandery and less territory than half a province; faced with a ruler who had received the Mandate and an age of peace, it could naturally have surrendered its soil and jade and begged to share the realm under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 乃複養喪家之疹，遵顛覆之軌，趑趄吳越，仍為匪民。

translations.literal: Yet again it nurtured the malady of a house in mourning, followed the track of overturning, hesitated like between Wu and Yue, and still remained unworthy subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Instead it nursed the sickness of a doomed house, followed the road to ruin, wavered like a man torn between Wu and Yue, and remained a rebellious people.

sentences.zh: 雖時屬大道，偃兵舞戚，然國家當混一之運，金陵是殄滅之期，有命不恆，斷可知矣。

translations.literal: Though the time belonged to the Great Way, with weapons laid aside and axes danced in peace, yet the state was at the destiny of unification and Jinling was the term of extermination. The mandate is not constant— clearly it can be foreseen.
translations.idiomatic: Though the age belonged to the Great Way, when arms were stilled and peace reigned, the empire was still bound for unification and Jinling was marked for destruction. Heaven's mandate does not linger forever—the outcome was plain to see.

sentences.zh: 房風之戮，元龜匪遙；

translations.literal: The execution of Fangfeng— the omen tortoise is not far off;
translations.idiomatic: Fangfeng's punishment foretold it; the tortoise omen was not far away;

sentences.zh: 孫皓之侯，守株難得。

translations.literal: Sun Hao's marquisate— waiting by the stump for a rabbit would be hard to obtain.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao's fate as a marquis showed that waiting idly by the tree stump for luck would avail them nothing.

sentences.zh: 迷而未覺，諒可湣焉。

translations.literal: Deluded and still unaware— truly one may pity them.
translations.idiomatic: They were lost and did not awaken— one can only pity them.

sentences.zh: 斯故未辯玄天之心，不聞君子之論也。

translations.literal: This is because they had not distinguished the heart of dark heaven and had not heard the discourse of the gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: This is because they failed to discern Heaven's hidden will and never heeded the counsel of the wise.

sentences.zh: 德林自隋有天下，每贊平陳之計。

translations.literal: From the time Sui possessed all under heaven, Delin always advocated plans for pacifying Chen.
translations.idiomatic: From the day Sui won the empire, Delin consistently urged a campaign to pacify Chen.

sentences.zh: 八年，車駕幸同州，德林以疾不從。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the imperial carriage visited Tongzhou; Delin, due to illness, did not accompany it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, when the emperor traveled to Tongzhou, Delin did not go with him because of illness.

sentences.zh: 敕書追之，書後御筆注雲：「伐陳事意，宜自隨也。

translations.literal: An edict letter pursued him; after the letter the emperor's own hand annotated: "Regarding the plan to attack Chen, you ought to come yourself."
translations.idiomatic: An imperial summons was sent after him, and the emperor added in his own hand: "As for the plan to attack Chen, you should come in person."

sentences.zh: 」時高熲因使入京，上語熲曰：「德林若患未堪行，宜自至宅，取其方略。

translations.literal: At that time Gao Jiong came to the capital on an errand; the emperor told Gao Jiong: "If Delin's illness makes travel impossible, go to his residence yourself and take his strategy."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Gao Jiong came to the capital on business, and the emperor told him: "If Delin is too ill to travel, go to his house yourself and obtain his plan."

sentences.zh: 」高祖以之付晉王廣。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu entrusted this to Prince of Jin Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu relayed this instruction to Prince Jin Guang.

sentences.zh: 後從駕還，在途中，高祖以馬鞭南指雲：「待平陳訖，會以七寶裝嚴公，使自山東無及之者。

translations.literal: Later, accompanying the carriage back, on the road Gaozu pointed south with his horse whip and said: "When Chen is pacified, I will certainly adorn you with the seven treasures so that none east of the mountains can match you."
translations.idiomatic: Later, on the return journey, Gaozu pointed south with his whip and said: "When Chen is conquered, I shall honor you with the seven treasures so that no one east of the mountains can equal you."

sentences.zh: 」及陳平，授柱國、郡公，實封八百戶，賞物三千段。

translations.literal: When Chen was pacified, he was granted Pillar of the State and Duke of a commandery, with a substantive fief of eight hundred households and a reward of three thousand rolls of goods.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen was pacified, he was made Pillar of the State and Duke of a commandery, with an enfeoffment of eight hundred households and a reward of three thousand bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 晉王廣已宣敕訖，有人說高熲曰：「天子畫策，晉王及諸將戮力之所致也。

translations.literal: Prince of Jin Guang had already proclaimed the edict when someone said to Gao Jiong: "The Son of Heaven devised the strategy; it was achieved through the Prince of Jin and the generals' joint effort."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jin Guang had already read out the edict when someone said to Gao Jiong: "The emperor devised the strategy; the victory was won by the Prince of Jin and the generals working together."

sentences.zh: 今乃歸功於李德林，諸將必當憤惋，且後世觀公有若虛行。

translations.literal: Now to ascribe the merit to Li Delin— the generals will surely be indignant and resentful, and posterity will view you, sir, as having gone through empty motions."
translations.idiomatic: To give the credit to Li Delin now will surely anger the generals, and later ages will think you, sir, played no real part."

sentences.zh: 」熲入言之，高祖乃止。

translations.literal: Gao Jiong entered and spoke of it; Gaozu then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong went in and said this, and Gaozu then halted the proclamation.

sentences.zh: 初，大象末，高祖以逆人王謙宅賜之，文書已出，至地官府，忽複改賜崔謙。

translations.literal: Initially, at the end of the Daxiang reign era, Gaozu bestowed upon him the residence of the rebel Wang Qian; the document had already been issued and reached the Land Office when suddenly it was changed to bestow on Cui Qian instead.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, at the end of the Daxiang era, Gaozu had granted him the house of the rebel Wang Qian; the order had already been issued and reached the Land Office when it was suddenly changed and given to Cui Qian instead.

sentences.zh: 上語德林曰：「夫人欲得，將與其舅。

translations.literal: The emperor told Delin: "The lady wanted it— I was going to give it to her uncle."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Delin: "My consort wanted the house; I was going to give it to her uncle."

sentences.zh: 於公無形跡，不須爭之，可自選一好宅。

translations.literal: You have no tangible claim on it; need not contest it— you may yourself choose a fine residence."
translations.idiomatic: You have no prior claim to it, so do not dispute the matter; choose another fine house for yourself."

sentences.zh: 若不稱意，當為營造，並覓莊店作替。

translations.literal: If it does not suit you, I shall have one built for you, and also find estate shops as compensation."
translations.idiomatic: If it does not please you, I will have one built for you and find shop properties as compensation."

sentences.zh: 」德林乃奏取逆人高阿那肱衛國縣市店八十塸為王謙宅替。

translations.literal: Delin then memorialized to take eighty market shops of Weiguo county belonging to the rebel Gao Anagong as replacement for Wang Qian's residence.
translations.idiomatic: Delin then memorialized to take eighty market shops in Weiguo county that had belonged to the rebel Gao Anagong as compensation for Wang Qian's house.

sentences.zh: 九年，車駕幸晉陽，店人上表訴稱：「地是民物，高氏強奪，於內造舍。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, the imperial carriage visited Jinyang; shopkeepers submitted petitions complaining: "The land is people's property; the Gao family seized it by force and built structures within."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, when the emperor visited Jinyang, the shopkeepers submitted petitions saying: "The land belongs to the people; the Gao family seized it by force and built on it."

sentences.zh: 」上命有司料還價直。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the relevant offices to calculate and return the price.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the authorities to calculate and repay its value.

sentences.zh: 遇追蘇威自長安至，奏雲：「高阿那肱是亂世宰相，以諂媚得幸，枉取民地，造店賃之。

translations.literal: It happened that Su Wei was summoned from Chang'an and arrived; he memorialized: "Gao Anagong was a minister of chaotic times who gained favor through flattery; he wrongly seized people's land, built shops and rented them out."
translations.idiomatic: Just then Su Wei was recalled from Chang'an and arrived; he memorialized: "Gao Anagong was a minister of troubled times who won favor through flattery, seized people's land without cause, built shops, and rented them out."

sentences.zh: 德林誣誷，妄奏自入。

translations.literal: Delin deceived and slandered, falsely memorializing to take them for himself."
translations.idiomatic: Delin lied and falsely memorialized to take the property for himself."

sentences.zh: 」李圓通、馮世基等又進雲：「此店收利如食千戶，請計日追贓。

translations.literal: Li Yuantong, Feng Shiji and others further submitted: "The income from these shops is like feeding off a thousand households; we request daily calculation to recover the illicit gains."
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuantong, Feng Shiji, and others further submitted: "The profit from these shops equals the income of a thousand households; we ask that the illicit gains be recovered day by day."

sentences.zh: 」上因責德林，德林請勘逆人文簿及本換宅之意，上不聽，乃悉追店給所住者。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore reproached Delin; Delin requested examination of rebel property registers and the original intent of the residence exchange, but the emperor would not listen and ordered all shops recovered and given to their occupants.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked Delin; Delin asked that rebel property registers and the original terms of the house exchange be investigated, but the emperor refused and ordered all the shops confiscated and returned to their occupants.

sentences.zh: 自是益嫌之。

translations.literal: From this he grew even more suspicious of him.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the emperor disliked him all the more.

sentences.zh: 十年，虞慶則等於關東諸道巡省使還，並奏雲：「五百家鄉正，專理辭訟，不便於民。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Yu Qingze and others returned from inspection commissions in the eastern passes and all memorialized: "The district heads over five hundred households exclusively handle litigation— it is inconvenient for the people."
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, Yu Qingze and others returned from inspection tours in the eastern passes and all memorialized: "The heads of five-hundred-household districts who handle lawsuits exclusively are a burden on the people."

sentences.zh: 黨與愛憎，公行貨賄。

translations.literal: Faction and favoritism; bribery openly practiced."
translations.idiomatic: They play favorites through cliques and take bribes openly."

sentences.zh: 」上仍令廢之。

translations.literal: The emperor still ordered their abolition.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the system abolished.

sentences.zh: 德林複奏雲：「此事臣本以為不可。

translations.literal: Delin again memorialized: "This matter I originally considered improper."
translations.idiomatic: Delin memorialized again: "Your servant originally thought this policy unwise."

sentences.zh: 然置來始爾，複即停廢，政令不一，朝成暮毀，深非帝王設法之義。

translations.literal: Yet having just been established, it is immediately suspended and abolished; policies are inconsistent, made in the morning and destroyed at evening— deeply contrary to the meaning of a sovereign establishing law."
translations.idiomatic: Yet it was only just established and is already being abolished; laws are inconsistent, made in the morning and undone at night—this is far from how an emperor should govern."

sentences.zh: 臣望陛下若于律令輒欲改張，即以軍法從事。

translations.literal: "Your servant hopes that if Your Majesty wishes to alter laws and decrees at will, he will be dealt with by military law."
translations.idiomatic: "Your servant asks that whenever Your Majesty wishes to change a law or decree on impulse, he be dealt with by military law."

sentences.zh: 不然者，紛紜未已。

translations.literal: Otherwise, confusion will not cease."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the turmoil will never end."

sentences.zh: 」高祖遂發怒，大詬雲：「爾欲將我作王莽邪？

translations.literal: Gaozu then grew angry and cursed greatly: "Do you wish to make me into Wang Mang?"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu flew into a rage and shouted: "Do you mean to make me another Wang Mang?"

sentences.zh: 」初，德林稱父為太尉諮議，以取贈官，李元操與陳茂等陰奏之曰：「德林之父終於校書，妄稱諮議。

translations.literal: Initially, Delin had styled his father as Staff Adviser to the Grand Commandant in order to obtain a posthumous office; Li Yuancao and Chen Mao and others secretly memorialized: "Delin's father ended as collator of texts yet falsely claimed the title of staff adviser."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Delin had styled his father Staff Adviser to the Grand Commandant in order to obtain a posthumous office; Li Yuancao, Chen Mao, and others secretly memorialized: "Delin's father ended his career as a collator of texts, yet Delin falsely claimed he had been a staff adviser."

sentences.zh: 」上甚銜之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply harbored resentment over this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply resented this.

sentences.zh: 至是，複庭議忤意，因數之曰：「公為內史，典朕機密，比不可豫計議者，以公不弘耳。

translations.literal: At this time, again in court discussion he went against the emperor's wishes; the emperor therefore reckoned against him: "You serve as Inner Secretary, managing my secrets— the reason you are not to participate in planning lately is because you are not magnanimous."
translations.idiomatic: Now, when he again contradicted the emperor in court debate, the emperor counted his faults against him: "You serve as Inner Secretary and hold my secrets; the reason you have lately been excluded from planning is that you lack breadth of mind."

sentences.zh: 寧自知乎？

translations.literal: Do you know this yourself?"
translations.idiomatic: Do you understand that?"

sentences.zh: 朕方以孝治天下，恐斯道廢闕，故立五教以弘之。

translations.literal: I am just now governing all under heaven through filial piety, fearing this Way may be abandoned and lacking, therefore establishing the Five Teachings to expand it."
translations.idiomatic: I am governing the realm through filial piety, fearing that this virtue may be lost, and so I established the Five Teachings to promote it."

sentences.zh: 公言孝由天性，何須設教。

translations.literal: You say filial piety comes from inborn nature— what need is there to establish teachings?"
translations.idiomatic: You said filial piety comes from inborn nature and asked what need there is to establish teachings."

sentences.zh: 然則孔子不當說《孝經》也。

translations.literal: In that case Confucius ought not to have expounded the Classic of Filial Piety."
translations.idiomatic: Then Confucius should never have written the Classic of Filial Piety."

sentences.zh: 又誷冒取店，妄加父官，朕實忿之而未能發。

translations.literal: Again deceiving and seizing shops, falsely adding to your father's title— I was truly resentful yet could not vent it."
translations.idiomatic: Then there was your fraud in seizing the shops and falsely inflating your father's rank—I have been angry about that but held my tongue."

sentences.zh: 今當以一州相遣耳。

translations.literal: Now I shall send you off with one province."
translations.idiomatic: Now I am sending you away to govern a province."

sentences.zh: 」因出為湖州刺史。

translations.literal: He was therefore dispatched as governor of Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was accordingly sent out as governor of Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 德林拜謝曰：「臣不敢複望內史令，請預散參。

translations.literal: Delin bowed and thanked him: "Your servant dare not again hope for the post of Inner Secretary; I request only to be permitted irregular attendance."
translations.idiomatic: Delin bowed and thanked him: "Your servant no longer dares hope for the post of Inner Secretary; I ask only to attend court on an irregular basis."

sentences.zh: 待陛下登封告成，一觀盛禮，然後收拙丘園，死且不恨。

translations.literal: "Wait until Your Majesty completes the feng and shan sacrifices and I may witness the grand rites once, then withdraw in clumsy retirement to hills and gardens— I would die without regret."
translations.idiomatic: "Wait until Your Majesty completes the feng and shan sacrifices and I have witnessed that great ceremony, then let me retire in obscurity to my hills and gardens—I would die content."

sentences.zh: 」上不許，轉懷州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor did not permit it and transferred him to be governor of Huai province.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused and transferred him to be governor of Huai province.

sentences.zh: 在州逢亢旱，課民掘井溉田，空致勞擾，竟無補益，為考司所貶。

translations.literal: In the province he encountered severe drought, levied the people to dig wells and irrigate fields— only causing empty labor and distress, ultimately without benefit— and was demoted by the evaluation office.
translations.idiomatic: While in office he encountered severe drought and ordered the people to dig wells and irrigate the fields; the effort brought only hardship and no benefit, and the evaluation office demoted him.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，卒官，時年六十一。

translations.literal: After somewhat more than a year, he died in office at age sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he died in office, at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈大將軍、廉州刺史，諡曰文。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Grand General and Governor of Lianzhou; posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Grand General and Governor of Lianzhou, with the posthumous name Wen.

sentences.zh: 及將葬，敕令羽林百人，並鼓吹一部，以給喪事。

translations.literal: When he was about to be buried, an edict ordered a hundred Imperial Guard soldiers and one complete ensemble of court music to be supplied for the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: When his burial was at hand, an edict ordered a hundred Imperial Guard soldiers and a full band of court music to be provided for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 贈物三百段，粟千石，祭乙太牢。

translations.literal: There were bestowed three hundred sections of goods, a thousand shi of grain, and sacrifice with great offerings of the second grade.
translations.idiomatic: The court gave three hundred bolts of goods, a thousand shi of grain, and a funeral sacrifice of the grandest grade.

sentences.zh: 德林美容儀，善談吐，齊天統中，兼中書侍郎，于賓館受國書。

translations.literal: Delin had a fine countenance and bearing and excelled at discourse; during Qi Tiantong he concurrently served as Secretariat Vice Director and at the guest house received state letters.
translations.idiomatic: Delin was handsome in bearing and skilled in speech; during Northern Qi's Tiantong era, as secretariat vice director he received foreign envoys' state letters at the guest house.

sentences.zh: 陳使江總目送之曰：「此即河朔之英靈也。

translations.literal: The Chen envoy Jiang Zong watched him depart with his eyes and said: "This is the heroic spirit of the north of the Yellow River."
translations.idiomatic: The Chen envoy Jiang Zong watched him go and said, "There is the finest spirit of the north country."

sentences.zh: 」器量沉深，時人未能測，唯任城王湝、趙彥深、魏收、陸遝大相欽重，延譽之言，無所不及。

translations.literal: His capacity and measure were deep and profound; men of the age could not fathom him—only Prince of Rencheng Jian, Zhao Yanshen, Wei Shou, and Lu Ang greatly esteemed him, and words of extended praise reached everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: His depth of character was hard for contemporaries to read; only Prince Jian of Rencheng, Zhao Yanshen, Wei Shou, and Lu Ang held him in the highest regard, and praise of him spread everywhere.

sentences.zh: 德林少孤，未有字，魏收謂之曰：「識度天才，必至公輔，吾輒以此字卿。

translations.literal: Delin was orphaned young and had no courtesy name; Wei Shou said to him: "Your insight and measure are heaven-sent talent—you will surely reach the highest ministerial rank; I therefore take this as your courtesy name."
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, Delin had no courtesy name; Wei Shou told him, "Your talent and vision will carry you to the highest office—I give you the name Gongfu for it."

sentences.zh: 」從官以後，即典機密，性重慎，嘗雲古人不言溫樹，何足稱也。

translations.literal: After he followed in office he at once administered secrets; his nature was heavily cautious, and he once said that the ancients did not speak of the warm tree—what is there to boast of?
translations.idiomatic: Once in office he handled secrets at once; deeply cautious by nature, he said the ancients did not discuss the locust tree in Huo Guang's garden—what virtue was there in boasting of discretion?

sentences.zh: 少以才學見知，及位望稍高，頗傷自任，爭名之徒，更相譖毀，所以運屬興王，功參佐命，十餘年間竟不徙級。

translations.literal: In youth he was known through talent and learning; when rank and standing grew somewhat high, he was rather wounded in self-reliance, and those contending for fame slandered one another—thus though fortune belonged to the rising king and his merit shared in assisting the mandate, over more than ten years he was never transferred in grade.
translations.idiomatic: Known early for learning, he grew somewhat self-important as his standing rose; rivals for fame slandered him repeatedly—so though he served a founding emperor and helped win the throne, for more than ten years his rank never advanced.

sentences.zh: 所撰文集，勒成八十卷，遭亂亡失，見五十卷行於世。

translations.literal: The collected writings he composed were compiled into eighty scrolls; lost in the disorders, fifty scrolls circulate in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings ran to eighty scrolls; most were lost in the turmoil, and fifty scrolls survive in circulation.

sentences.zh: 敕撰《齊史》未成。

translations.literal: Ordered to compile the History of Qi, he did not finish.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to compile the History of Qi but did not complete it.

sentences.zh: 子 百藥有子曰百藥，博涉多才，詞藻清贍。

translations.literal: Son: Baoyao. Baoyao was broadly learned and multitalented, his diction clear and rich.
translations.idiomatic: His son Baoyao was broadly learned and multitalented, with clear and ample literary style.

sentences.zh: 釋巾太子通事舍人，後遷太子舍人、尚書禮部員外郎，襲爵安平縣公，桂州司馬。

translations.literal: Removing his scarf he served as the Crown Prince's Attendant Master of Affairs; later he was transferred to Crown Prince Attendant, Supernumerary Bureau Director of the Ministry of Rites, inherited the noble rank of Duke of Anping county, and became Military Administrator of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as attendant master of affairs to the crown prince, then became crown prince attendant, supernumerary director in the Ministry of Rites, inherited the dukedom of Anping, and was made military administrator of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 煬帝惡其初不附己，以為步兵校尉。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang resented that at first he did not attach himself to him and made him Vice Colonel of Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang disliked his early refusal to side with him and demoted him to vice colonel of footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 大業末，轉建安郡丞。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye he was transferred to Assistant Administrator of Jian'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Daye he was made assistant administrator of Jian'an commandery.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰史臣曰：德林幼有操尚，學富才優，譽重鄴中，聲飛關右。

translations.literal: The historian says: Delin from youth had moral resolve, learning rich and talent excellent; his fame weighed heavy in Ye, his reputation flying west of the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Delin showed moral resolve from youth, with rich learning and outstanding talent; his fame was great in Ye and his reputation spread through the northwest.

sentences.zh: 王基締構，協贊謀猷，羽檄交馳，絲綸間發，文誥之美，時無與二。

translations.literal: When the royal foundation was being tied together, he assisted in planning stratagems; feathered proclamations raced back and forth, silk edicts issued in succession—the beauty of his literary proclamations, none second in the age.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial foundation was laid he helped shape its strategy; as dispatches and edicts flew without cease, the elegance of his prose had no peer in his time.

sentences.zh: 君臣體合，自致青雲，不患莫己知，豈徒言也！

translations.literal: Lord and minister joined in body and harmony, reaching the blue clouds by themselves—not fearing that none would know them—is this merely empty talk!
translations.idiomatic: Ruler and minister were perfectly matched and rose together to the heights—this was no empty boast that talent need never fear going unknown!
